recent_videos.title: WHAT WORKS FOR HER MAY NOT WORK FOR YOU 😢 | A Powerful Life Lesson#shorts
recent_videos.description:
Bisi watched her neighbour, Mama Grace, making money from selling food and assumed she could achieve the same success. She sold everything in her plastic goods shop and started selling food, believing money would come easily.
But reality taught her a painful lesson.
An elderly woman helped her understand that she had seen Mama Grace’s success but had never seen her struggles, sacrifices, and years of hard work.
The lesson? Don't compare your journey with another person's success. Learn from others, appreciate what you have, and discover what works for you.
Everyone has a different journey, different strengths, and different opportunities. Never abandon your own path simply because someone else's life looks better.
Watch till the end and share this story with someone who needs this reminder.
Vivian Stories — Stories That Touch the Heart.

recent_videos.title: THE WIFE IS NOT HIS ROOMMATE! 😳💔 | He Promised Her Marriage, Then Called Her a Stranger#shorts
recent_videos.description:
He told his girlfriend that his wife was nothing more than his roommate. He promised her marriage, kissed her hand, and made her believe she was the woman he truly wanted.

But when his pregnant wife suddenly appeared, everything changed. The same man who had promised her heaven and earth suddenly called her a stranger!

Shocked and heartbroken, she finally realised the truth: she had been believing the promises of a man who was already deceiving his own wife.

Ladies, please open your eyes! When a married man tells you his wife is only his roommate, don’t just believe his words. Watch his actions.

If he can deceive the woman he married, what makes you think his promises to you are different?

Watch till the end and share this story with someone who needs this reminder.

Follow Vivian Stories for more emotional stories with powerful life lessons.

recent_videos.title: DADDY, I WILL NEVER MARRY A MAN LIKE YOU | A Powerful Parenting Story..shorts
recent_videos.description:
A father provides for his family and expects everyone to obey him. His wife is rarely allowed to speak, disagree, or express her feelings.

But one day, his daughter says something that leaves him speechless:

“Daddy, I will never marry a man like you.”

What made her say those words? And what has she been learning from watching her parents?

This emotional Nigerian family story explores parenting, marriage, respect, and the powerful influence parents have on their children’s future relationships.

Children don’t learn only from our advice. They also learn from our actions, our attitudes, and the way we treat the people we claim to love.

What are you teaching your children without saying a word?

Watch until the end and share your thoughts in the comments.

recent_videos.title: THE MAN WHO HAD NOTHING | A Powerful Nigerian Movie About Love, Poverty & Hope..shorts
recent_videos.description:
What happens when the man you love has nothing to offer you but his dreams?

Tony was intelligent, hardworking, and full of ideas, but life seemed determined to keep him down. With no parents, no money, and no one to turn to, his dreams slowly became a painful reminder of everything he could not provide.

Grace chose to stand by him despite her mother’s warnings. But as poverty tightened its grip on their family, even their love was pushed to its breaking point.

When hunger, humiliation, and hopelessness threatened to destroy everything they had built, Tony began to wonder if his life would ever change.

Then, through an unexpected encounter, a new opportunity appeared.

THE MAN WHO HAD NOTHING is an emotional Nigerian drama about love, sacrifice, poverty, determination, faith, and the power of never giving up.

Sometimes, the person everyone looks down on is only one opportunity away from changing their story.

Watch until the end, and tell us what you would have done in Grace’s position.

❤️ What is your biggest lesson from this story? Share your thoughts in the comments.

If this story touches your heart, please LIKE, SHARE, and SUBSCRIBE to Vivian Stories for more emotional stories that inspire, teach, and remind us that life can change when we least expect it.

recent_videos.description:

recent_videos.description:
Cyberbullying: What Parents Should Do If Their Child Is Being Bullied Online | Crayons Clinics

Cyberbullying can happen through social media, messaging apps, online games and mobile phones. It may involve repeated hurtful messages, threats, spreading rumours, sharing embarrassing photos or pretending to be someone else online. It can affect a child's emotional wellbeing, confidence, sleep, friendships and school performance.

Dr. Aakanksha Singh and Dr. Rakesh Sharma from Crayons Clinics share practical guidance to help parents recognise cyberbullying and support their child.

SIGNS YOUR CHILD MAY BE EXPERIENCING CYBERBULLYING

- Becoming upset, sad or angry during or after using devices.
- Withdrawing from family, friends or favourite activities.
- Feeling nervous when messages arrive or suddenly switching off devices.
- Experiencing unexplained headaches, stomach aches, sleep difficulties or appetite changes.
- Losing interest in school or showing a decline in academic performance.

9 STEPS PARENTS CAN TAKE

1. Stay calm, listen and reassure your child that the bullying is not their fault. Thank them for telling you and avoid blaming them.

2. Save the evidence before anything is deleted. Take screenshots of messages, posts and profiles, including dates, times and usernames. Save links, emails and voice notes securely.

3. Do not reply or retaliate. Encourage your child not to respond to, forward or share hurtful content.

4. Block, restrict and report the person using the platform's safety tools. Help your child complete these steps.

5. Review privacy and security settings. Limit who can contact or tag your child, change passwords if needed and avoid sharing personal information online.

6. Inform the school if other students are involved. Share the saved evidence and ask what action will be taken and when.

7. Report serious cases to the police or cybercrime authorities, particularly when threats, blackmail, private images, impersonation or persistent harassme

recent_videos.description:
My Emotional Ladder: Helping Autistic Children Understand Big Feelings | Crayons Clinics

Children may find it difficult to recognise, describe and manage intense emotions. The My Emotional Ladder worksheet from Crayons Clinics helps autistic children aged approximately 5 to 10 identify their feelings, notice body signals and choose calming strategies with support from a parent or trusted adult.

Developed by Dr. Aakanksha Singh, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, this printable worksheet uses a five-point scale to help children communicate how they feel before emotions become overwhelming.

HOW THE FIVE-POINT EMOTIONAL LADDER WORKS

Level 1 - Calm: The body feels relaxed and ready to play or learn. Encourage the child to notice what calm feels like.

Level 2 - A Little Bothered: The child may feel slightly tense, fidgety or have a small frown. Stretching, sipping water or using reassuring self-talk may help.

Level 3 - Wobbly: The child may feel restless, notice a faster heartbeat or experience worried thoughts. Try five slow breaths, count to ten or encourage the child to tell a grown-up, "I am at a 3."

Level 4 - Very Upset: The child may have a hot face, tight tummy, clenched fists or difficulty listening. Offer a break, headphones, a squeeze ball or a quieter space.

Level 5 - Overwhelmed: The child may feel shaky or intensely distressed, cry or shout, and find it difficult to think. Prioritise safety and quiet, stay nearby and use very few words. Save questions and teaching for when the child is calm.

HOW PARENTS CAN USE THE EMOTIONAL LADDER

1. Complete the worksheet together when your child is calm, not during a meltdown.
2. Let your child choose the words, colours and drawings that make sense to them.
3. Ask, "What does your body feel like?" and "What helps you?"
4. Use neutral language. No emotional level is good or bad.
5. Check in daily, such as after school, and praise your child for recognising feelings early.
6. Practise calming strategies at lower lev

recent_videos.description:
How do you know if your teenager is depressed or just going through normal teenage mood swings? What are the warning signs of depression in teenagers, and how can parents help a teen struggling with depression?

Teenagers go through emotional, physical and social changes. But when your teen seems persistently sad, irritated, withdrawn, unmotivated or no longer interested in activities they once enjoyed, it may be more than typical teenage behaviour.

Teen depression is a real mental health condition, and recognising the early signs can make a significant difference.

In this video, Dr. Aakanksha Singh, Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist and Founder of Crayons Clinics, explains how parents can recognise depression in teenagers, understand the connection between autism and depression, support their teen's emotional wellbeing and know when professional mental health care is necessary.

6 Warning Signs of Depression in Teenagers: How can you tell if your teenager has depression? Look for persistent changes in their usual behaviour, mood and daily functioning.

Not every teenager with depression appears visibly sad. Some may primarily show irritability, anger, withdrawal or behavioural changes.

Autism and Depression: Why Are Autistic Teenagers at Higher Risk?

Autistic teenagers can experience a higher risk of depression due to challenges such as:

• Social exhaustion and difficulties navigating friendships  
• Masking autistic traits to fit into social environments  
• Peer rejection, bullying or social isolation  
• Emotional and sensory overwhelm  

Depression in autistic teenagers can be difficult to recognise because some symptoms overlap with existing autistic characteristics.

How Can Parents Help a Teenager With Depression? If symptoms persist for two weeks or more, worsen, or significantly affect school, relationships or daily functioning, arrange a professional assessment. Seek help sooner if symptoms are severe.

recent_videos.description:
Top Autism Tests: How Is Autism Diagnosed in Children? | Crayons Clinics

Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is diagnosed through developmental history, behavioural observation and a comprehensive clinical assessment. There is no single blood test that can confirm autism. Understanding the assessment process helps parents recognise why different screening tools and diagnostic methods may be used.

M-CHAT-R/F: EARLY AUTISM SCREENING

The Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, Revised with Follow-Up (M-CHAT-R/F) is a screening tool used to identify possible early signs of autism in young children. A positive screening result does not confirm an autism diagnosis and may indicate the need for further evaluation.

ADOS-2: STRUCTURED BEHAVIOURAL OBSERVATION

The Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, Second Edition (ADOS-2), involves structured activities and interactions conducted by a trained professional. The child's communication, social interaction and behaviour are observed as part of the assessment.

ADI-R: DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY INTERVIEW

The Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) is a detailed interview with parents or caregivers. It gathers information about the child's developmental history and behaviours to support the diagnostic process.

OTHER ASSESSMENTS THAT MAY BE RECOMMENDED

Depending on the child's individual needs, professionals may recommend hearing tests, genetic testing or neurological evaluation to investigate other conditions or associated developmental concerns.

WHY IS A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT IMPORTANT?

No single test or checklist can independently confirm autism. Diagnosis involves considering developmental history, behavioural observations and clinical findings. A qualified professional or multidisciplinary team can help understand the child's individual strengths, developmental needs and appropriate support options.

recent_videos.title: Stress Vs Anxiety #ytshorts #anxiety #stress #awareness
recent_videos.description:
Stress vs. Anxiety: How to Recognise the Difference and What to Do | Crayons Clinics

Do you feel overwhelmed, tense, restless or worried even when everything seems fine? Stress and anxiety can share symptoms such as a racing heart, tight chest, difficulty sleeping and a mind that will not switch off. However, understanding the difference can help you choose the right next step.

Dr. Aakanksha Singh and Dr. Rakesh Sharma from Crayons Clinics explain how to recognise stress and anxiety, manage symptoms and know when to seek professional support.

STRESS VS. ANXIETY: WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE?

Stress is usually a response to an identifiable pressure, such as work deadlines, exams, financial concerns, arguments, moving or illness. It often eases when the situation is resolved.

Anxiety involves ongoing worry, fear or unease that may continue even after a stressful situation has passed. It can also appear when there is no obvious trigger.

Common signs of stress include:
- Feeling pressured, overwhelmed or frustrated
- Muscle tension and headaches
- Poor sleep and an upset stomach
- Irritability

Common signs of anxiety include:
- Persistent worry, dread or fear
- Restlessness and difficulty concentrating
- Tingling sensations or a feeling that something bad may happen
- Sleep difficulties and physical tension

Symptoms can overlap. Ask yourself: Is there a clear cause, and does the feeling ease when the problem is addressed?

5 WAYS TO MANAGE STRESS

1. Identify the stressor. Write down what is weighing on you so you can see what needs attention.

2. Break tasks into smaller steps. Prioritise one or two important tasks for today instead of trying to solve everything at once.

3. Move your body. Even a 20-minute walk can help manage stress and support sleep.

4. Protect your sleep. Keep a consistent sleep and wake time and create a screen-free wind-down routine.

5. Ask for help. Reduce your workload where possible and talk to someone you trust.

6 WAYS TO MANAGE ANXIETY

recent_videos.title: daily life skills for ASD kids #ytshorts #autism #skills #independence
recent_videos.description:
Daily Living Skills at Every Age | Autism and Neurodivergent Children | Crayons Clinics

How can you help your autistic or neurodivergent child become more independent in everyday life? Skills such as dressing, eating, personal hygiene, communicating needs, managing money and travelling develop gradually, and every child follows a different timeline.

Dr. Aakanksha Singh from Crayons Clinics explains how parents can identify the next daily living skill to build and support independence without unnecessary pressure.

DAILY LIVING SKILLS BY AGE

Infants (0-24 months): Signalling needs through sounds or gestures, copying others, self-feeding small pieces and drinking from a cup.

Toddlers (2-4 years): Feeding themselves, pulling on a top, washing hands, brushing teeth with help, participating in dressing and toileting, and communicating needs through speech, signs or devices.

Children (5-12 years): Dressing, hygiene with reminders, showering, simple food preparation, tidying, basic safety, following checklists and two-step instructions. Older children may begin handling small amounts of money and completing chores with supervision.

Teenagers (13-18 years): Cooking, laundry, cleaning, grocery lists, budgeting, appointments, deadlines, public transport, self-advocacy, understanding consent and medicine safety.

Young adults (18+ years): Building skills to manage health, home, money, work and community life.

These are common patterns, not deadlines. Uneven development is normal.

6 WAYS TO BUILD DAILY LIVING SKILLS AT HOME

1. CHOOSE ONE NEXT SKILL
Identify the next small, achievable step instead of comparing your child with others.

2. TREAT EACH SKILL AREA SEPARATELY
Your child may be confident in one area and need support in another.

3. ALLOW TIME TO PRACTISE
Avoid taking over a task simply because it is slow or messy. Practice helps build independence.

4. USE VISUAL SUPPORTS
Checklists, prompts, visual schedules and step-by-step pictures can make routines easier.

recent_videos.description:
Supporting Your Child's Social Skills | A Step-by-Step Guide for Parents | Crayons Clinics

How can parents support an autistic child's social skills without pressure? Building social confidence starts with understanding your child's interests, respecting their communication style and creating comfortable opportunities for connection.

Dr. Aakanksha Singh from Crayons Clinics shares practical ways to support children's communication, social participation and emotional comfort.

5 WAYS TO SUPPORT YOUR CHILD'S SOCIAL SKILLS

1. FOLLOW YOUR CHILD'S INTERESTS
Join activities your child already enjoys, such as blocks, drawing, trains, puzzles, music or favourite books. Follow their lead and allow them to show you how they like to play. For example, add a block to their tower when invited or introduce a simple turn-taking game without taking over.

2. CREATE SMALL, COMFORTABLE OPPORTUNITIES
Start with familiar people, quieter places and short activities. One-to-one play may feel more manageable than a busy group. Offer breaks and stop if your child becomes overwhelmed. More exposure is not always better; comfort and the environment matter.

3. MODEL SOCIAL INTERACTION
Demonstrate taking turns, asking for help, sharing interests and using phrases such as "my turn" and "your turn." Keep language simple and give your child time to respond. School Anxiety in Autistic Children: A Parent Checklist | Crayons Clinics

Does your autistic child have meltdowns before school, refuse to attend school, complain of stomach aches, or become overwhelmed by changes in routine? These may be signs of school-related anxiety.

Dr. Aakanksha Singh, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, shares a practical guide from Crayons Clinics to help parents identify possible anxiety triggers and work with schools to support autistic children.

7 COMMON SCHOOL ANXIETY TRIGGERS

1. Change and unpredictability: Unexpected routine changes, substitute teachers, assemblies, waiting or too many demands.

2. Sensory experiences: Loud noises, bright lights, crowded spaces, strong smells, uncomfortable clothing or unexpected touch.

3. Social situations: Difficulty joining conversations, unclear social rules, group work, teasing, exclusion or bullying.

4. Transitions: Playground breaks, lunch, school bus journeys and moving between classrooms.

5. Schoolwork and performance: Multi-step tasks, tests, fear of mistakes, reading, writing or speaking in class.

6. Separation and fears: Being away from parents, worrying about collection arrangements or recent changes at home or school.

7. Home routines: Getting ready in the morning, packing the school bag, homework and bedtime routines.

HOW TO USE THE PARENT CHECKLIST AND TRACKER

Step 1: Tick the possible triggers that seem relevant to your child. A tick indicates a possible trigger, not a confirmed cause.

Step 2: Watch for signs of anxiety, including headaches, stomach aches, tiredness, increased meltdowns, withdrawal, sleep difficulties, irritability and repeated requests for reassurance.

Step 3: Record incidents for two to three weeks. Note the date, location, what happened before the anxiety, how your child showed distress and what helped.

Step 4: Look for patterns involving particular places, times, people or demands.

If Your Child Is Being Bullied: A Step-by-Step Guide for Parents | Crayons Clinics

Is your child suddenly refusing to go to school, becoming withdrawn, sleeping poorly or avoiding friends? These changes may be signs of bullying. Knowing how to respond calmly and support your child can make a difference.

Dr. Aakanksha Singh, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, shares a step-by-step guide from Crayons Clinics to help parents respond to bullying at home and work with the school.

10 STEPS PARENTS CAN TAKE WHEN A CHILD IS BEING BULLIED

1. CARE FOR YOUR CHILD FIRST
Listen calmly without interrupting or judging. Praise your child for telling you and reassure them that the bullying is not their fault. Check their immediate safety and seek professional help promptly if you are worried they may harm themselves or others.

2. GENTLY GATHER THE FACTS
Ask open questions such as, "What has been upsetting you at school?" Find out who is involved, what happened, where and when it occurred, and whether it involved physical behaviour, exclusion, rumours or online bullying.

3. KEEP A RECORD
Save messages, emails, voice notes and screenshots. Maintain a factual timeline of incidents, including dates, times, locations, people involved, witnesses and whom you reported the incident to.

4. MAKE A PLAN TOGETHER
Ask your child what would help them feel safer. Explain what you plan to do before taking action. Take threats of physical harm seriously and avoid promising an immediate solution.

5. CHECK THE SCHOOL'S ANTI-BULLYING POLICY
Look at the student handbook or school website to understand the reporting process and identify the person responsible for handling bullying concerns.

6. REPORT THE BULLYING TO THE SCHOOL

recent_videos.description:
Big Feelings Activity Cards for Children | Crayons Clinics

Helping children understand and manage big emotions starts with small, everyday activities. Children aged 3 to 8 can gradually learn to recognise feelings, calm their bodies, solve problems and manage transitions with support from parents and caregivers.

Crayons Clinics' Big Feelings Activity Cards, shared by Dr. Aakanksha Singh, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, offer 17 simple, low-cost activities that parents can practise at home.

Here are four ways to support your child's emotional development:

1. NAME THE FEELING
Use a feelings chart, mirror play, feelings charades, storytime questions, drawing or a feelings collage to help your child recognise and express emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, fear and frustration.

2. HELP YOUR CHILD CALM THEIR BODY
Try bubble breathing, a calm-down glitter jar, heavy-work activities, rhythm games, a calm-down dance party or simple yoga poses. Practise these strategies when your child is calm, so they become familiar when emotions run high.

3. PRACTISE EVERYDAY PROBLEM-SOLVING
Use toys and role-play to practise situations such as sharing, losing a game or feeling left out. When your child shares an emotion, listen without immediately trying to fix or dismiss it. Ask, "Tell me more about that."

4. CREATE A SUPPORTIVE HOME ENVIRONMENT
Set up a calm-down corner, use picture schedules and give transition warnings about five minutes and two minutes before a change. Celebrate small wins by noticing when your child takes a breath, asks for help or manages frustration.

IMPORTANT TIPS FOR PARENTS
- Practise when your child is calm, not during a meltdown.
- Keep activities short and playful. Five minutes can be enough.
- Follow your child's lead and skip activities that do not suit them.
- Model how you recognise and manage your own feelings.
- Never force a child to name a feeling or participate in an activity.

MAKE YOUR HOME EXAM-FRIENDLY
A message for parents
Assalamualaikum dear parents!
Examinations are around the corner, and today I want to speak to you about something very important.
We often talk about examination preparation in terms of what the school should do, what the teacher should do and what the child should do.
But there is another very important space that influences a child's learning every single day—
HOME.
And examinations, when looked at positively, are not meant to frighten our children.
They are an opportunity to understand where we stand, what we have understood, what needs improvement and where we need to put in more effort.

1. LOOK AT THE CHILD'S ROUTINE
Dear parents, please look at your child's daily routine.
Is your child waking up at a reasonable time?
Is your child sleeping on time?
Are there late-night conversations, television, mobile phones, gaming or social gatherings disturbing the routine?
Sleep is not a luxury that can be sacrificed during examinations.
Children aged 6–12 generally need around 9–12 hours of sleep, while adolescents aged 13–18 generally need 8–10 hours. Adequate sleep supports attention, concentration and readiness to learn.
So please don't say,
"Exams are coming. Let the child study till midnight!"
Sometimes, one hour of focused learning after adequate rest can be far more useful than several tired hours of studying.
And parents, please model the routine too.
If we expect our children to follow discipline, they need to see discipline around them.
2. PAY ATTENTION TO FOOD AND WATER
The next important area is nutrition.
A child who is studying needs energy.
Please provide nutritious, balanced meals at appropriate times. Avoid allowing examination preparation to become an excuse for irregular eating.
And don't forget water.

So—
Sleep well.
Eat well.
Drink enough water.
Then study well.

recent_videos.title: The Stay At Home Dilemma: “I Love My Children, But What About Me? Identity, Purpose & Starting Again
recent_videos.description:
What happens when you leave a successful corporate career to become a stay-at-home mom and years later realize you're ready for something more?

In this episode of my Stay-at-Home Mom series, I sit down with Helena to talk about the parts of leaving a career for motherhood that we don't always talk about: identity, financial independence, purpose, being present with your children, and figuring out who you are when one season of your life ends and another begins.

Helena shares what it really cost her to walk away from corporate life, what staying home allowed her to experience with her children, and how she knew when it was finally time to explore something beyond motherhood.

We also talk about how The Makeover Place was born, becoming an entrepreneur after being a stay-at-home mom, and how she now protects herself from recreating the same busyness she once walked away from.

If you're a stay-at-home mom wondering, “What comes next for me?” or a working mom questioning what success should look like in this season, I hope this conversation reminds you that your life can have many beautiful chapters.

In this conversation:
• Leaving a corporate career to become a stay-at-home mom
• Losing financial independence
• Identity after becoming a mother
• Being present during your children's early years
• Knowing when you're ready to work or build again
• Starting a business after a career break
• Motherhood and entrepreneurship
• Redefining success after children
• Finding purpose beyond your previous career

💬 QUESTION: If you've ever taken a career break for motherhood, what was the hardest part of the transition for you and did your definition of success change?

Subscribe for more honest conversations on motherhood, marriage, family, finances and building a meaningful life.

recent_videos.title: I Left My Career To Raise the Children| Was it Worth It? The Truth Every Mom Needs to Hear
recent_videos.description:
What really happens when a woman puts her career on pause to stay home and raise her children and what happens when she's finally ready to return?
In this episode, I sit down with @joan_spaces for an honest conversation about leaving her career to become a stay-at-home mom, navigating the loss of income and independence, wrestling with identity, watching other women progress professionally, and eventually finding her way back into work.
We talk about the beautiful parts of being present with your children, but also the parts of staying home that aren't talked about enough: feeling left behind, questioning your value outside of motherhood, financial adjustments, maintaining your skills and dreams, and wondering whether you'll ever be able to pick up your career again.
Joan also shares how she knew her stay-at-home season was coming to an end, the fears that came with returning to work, how she discovered interior design, and whether knowing everything she knows now she would make the same decision again.
We also tackle a difficult question many mothers wrestle with:
Can you pause a career and come back to it later? And if so, is returning really as easy as people make it sound?
Whether you're a stay-at-home mom who feels invisible, a working mom considering a career break, or a mother who wishes she could stay home but financially cannot, I hope this conversation gives you perspective, encouragement and grace for your own season.

recent_videos.title: From Career to Stay Home Mom to Building a Business While Staying Present With The Children
recent_videos.description:
What does it actually look like to leave corporate, become a stay-at-home mom, homeschool your children AND build a thriving business from home?

In episode two of my Stewarding the Stay-at-Home Mom Season series, I sit down with Diana Kagimba, founder of Ruby's Gift Store, to talk about the life she has intentionally built around motherhood, family and entrepreneurship.

Diana shares why she walked away from corporate life, how she and her husband navigated moving from two incomes to one, the reality of adjusting to being home full-time, and why she eventually chose to homeschool her children. But her story didn't stop with staying home. While raising and homeschooling her children, Diana built Ruby's Gift Store and eventually created systems that allow the business to function without requiring her presence in every day-to-day operation.

We talk about how she balances homeschooling, business, marriage, home and herself; what she has had to say “no” to; raising confident and independent children when you're a very present mother; and why she believes children don't necessarily need us less as they grow older, their needs simply change.

We also explore a bigger question: What does it mean for a woman to be fruitful when fruitfulness isn't always measured by a salary, promotion, degree or business?
Whether you're a stay-at-home mom, homeschooling mom, working mother, entrepreneur or simply trying to build a life around what matters most to you, I hope Diana's story gives you something to think about.

recent_videos.title: First look: SEA S Concourse #airportdesign #airports #airportnews #seattle #airportlook #airport
recent_videos.description:
Reimagining the 1970s-era international concourse at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) for the next generation of air travel.

The S Concourse Evolution project will transform the airport’s 1970s-era international concourse with 150,000 square feet of additional space, a new upper concourse level, enhanced dual-level boarding operations and expanded dining, retail and lounge space.

HOK’s design draws inspiration from the geography and cultural history of the Pacific Northwest, creating a more intuitive passenger experience while improving circulation, resilience and operational performance.

Targeting LEED Silver certification, the project is expected to reduce annual operational greenhouse gas emissions by 58% and energy use by 16% compared with Port of Seattle standards.

HOK is serving as lead designer in collaboration with prime consultant and lead architect AECOM. Major construction is scheduled to begin in 2027.

recent_videos.title: Expanding DFW through #modularconstruction #airport #airportdesign #airportlook #architects
recent_videos.description:
How do you expand one of the world’s busiest airports without disrupting operations?

At Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, HOK helped answer that question through modular design and construction. For the Terminal A and C pier expansions, up to 1,200-ton building modules were fabricated and partially fitted out outside the airport’s secure perimeter with mechanical systems, curtain wall glazing, and interior finishes already in place before being moved to their final locations.

These strategies reduced the construction timeline by 33%, maintained gate operations during construction, and added nine new gates that will help DFW accommodate future growth.

recent_videos.title: Celebrating #Worldskyscraperday #skyscraper #skyscrapers #tallbuildings #skyscraperdesign #architect
recent_videos.description:
Skyscrapers are dramatic. They’re powerful reminders of human ingenuity and evolution.
 
At their best, tall buildings concentrate people, activity and opportunity while creating landmarks that can define how a city is seen and experienced.
 
On #WorldSkyscraperDay, we’re celebrating the ambition behind building upward with a look at three unbuilt HOK-designed towers envisioned for Asia-Pacific:
 
Project 1 - Confidential Super Tall Mixed-use Project
 
This super tall mixed-use development in China creates an iconic new city center, strengthening Guangzhou’s position in the global market. The building’s sleek massing and silvery facade pay homage to Guangzhou’s historic fishing industry. Six hundred meters above ground, the tower’s tapering form culminates in a high-altitude atrium that provides breathtaking views of the city and the Pearl River.
 
Project 2 - E5 New Songdo City
 
In South Korea, Block E5 is the last prominent site to be developed along Central Park in New Songdo City. Two residential towers are conceived as organic twisting forms, with each floor plate designed to maximize views and shared amenities. Retail and commercial buildings anchor the development, while terraces overlooking Central Park and a courtyard offer residents and guests access to nature and private outdoor experiences.
 
Project 3 - Lend Lease Circular Quay
 
This design proposal creates a new city landmark and welcoming destination in Sydney, Australia. The 814-foot-tall tower has a distinct profile on the skyline while encouraging pedestrian movement through the site. An offset core preserves harbor and Sydney Opera House views, while an external structural shell supports office flexibility. The design integrates art within the architecture and designates plazas as public event spaces.
 
🔗 Explore more including exclusive BTS in HOK's book Tall Buildings, Vol. 2, available free for download and viewing, now.

recent_videos.title: Is It Milk Allergy or Lactose Intolerance? Know the Signs | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description:
Milk made the baby uncomfortable. Here is what parents need to know. This Aptaclub India Short takes one of the most confusing moments in early parenting, a baby who reacts badly after milk, and separates the two conditions that are most often mixed up: milk allergy and lactose intolerance. They can look similar from the outside, which is exactly why so many parents guess wrong, and why the difference is worth understanding before the next feed.
A milk allergy is a reaction of the immune system to the proteins in milk. Because the immune system is involved, the signs are not limited to the tummy. Parents may see skin symptoms, vomiting, diarrhoea and breathing symptoms. Lactose intolerance is a different thing altogether. Here the tummy has trouble digesting lactose, the sugar in milk, so what parents may see is gas, bloating and loose stools. The one sign that does not belong to lactose intolerance is breathing symptoms, and the Short makes that distinction deliberately clear, because it is often the detail that helps a parent tell the two apart.
That is also why the video does not end with a self diagnosis. Because symptoms can overlap, parents should let their paediatrician help work out which one it is. Vomiting, loose stools and an unsettled baby can appear in more than one situation, and the right next step depends on knowing whether this is baby allergies at work or a matter of baby digestion, with the tummy struggling to handle lactose. Baby digestive problems and allergic reactions call for different advice, and only a doctor can say which advice applies. A paediatrician can look at the whole picture, the symptoms, the timing and the baby's history, and arrive at an answer a worried parent cannot reach from a checklist alone.

recent_videos.title: What Goes Unseen Inside Your Baby’s Gut After Birth | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description:
A lot is happening inside a newborn that goes unseen. This Aptaclub India Short turns to one of those things: a developing gut. While parents watch for the visible milestones, the first smile, the first grasp, the first time a baby holds their head up, a quieter kind of growth is under way inside, and it matters just as much to how a baby takes in the world in the first months.
The gut barrier starts developing from birth and continues to mature as a baby grows. It does not arrive finished. With time, it learns to support the baby better, taking in the good things their body needs, the vitamins and minerals that fuel growth, while keeping unwanted elements out. That gradual maturing is the heart of baby gut health in the early months, and it is why gut health is talked about so often alongside immunity and infant health and development: the gut is where a great deal of what a baby needs is absorbed, and where a great deal of protection begins.
The last line of the Short is the one for parents to hold on to. Every feed is a part of their growing journey. Each feed is not just a meal, it is another step in how the gut learns and strengthens, and in how a baby's body builds the foundations it will rely on later. For a parent in the repetitive rhythm of early baby feeding, that is a useful way to see it: the routine is doing quiet, important work, even on the days when it feels like nothing more than another bottle or another feed at 2am. Growth that cannot be seen is still growth, and every feed is adding to it.
Aptaclub India brings paediatricians and parents together on exactly these questions, from gut health and baby gut health to baby feeding, baby immunity and the everyday concerns of early parenting. Through Apta Expert, parents get doctor led parenting tips in plain language, so the unseen side of a baby's growth is understood rather than guessed at. recent_videos.title: Baby Sleep Regression Is Real: Why Your Routine Did Not Fail | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description:
The minute she thought they had finally cracked sleep, everything changed. In this Aptaclub India Short, a mother shares the moment so many parents recognise: bedtime had become easier, her daughter was sleeping longer, and she had allowed herself to believe that the routine was finally working. Then, without warning, the night wakings returned. Naps became unpredictable, bedtime became a struggle, and the progress she had been so relieved about seemed to disappear overnight.
What followed was the questioning. Is she hungry? Is the bedtime wrong? Did I somehow ruin the routine? Every parent who has watched a working routine fall apart knows that spiral, and it is the most honest part of this story. When baby sleep changes suddenly, the instinct is to look for the mistake, and the mistake is almost always assumed to be the parent's own, never the baby's growth. This mother went through every possibility before she found the explanation that actually fit.
That explanation was sleep regression. Baby sleep does not always improve in one straight line. As babies grow and go through developmental changes, sleep patterns can change for a while, and what looks like a step backwards is often a sign that something is moving forward. Growth can change sleep too. Learning this is what shifted her view of the whole situation: they were not back at zero, they were simply going through another phase. For a parent in the middle of a week of broken nights, that is the difference between despair and patience, because a phase has an end, and baby sleep problems that arrive alongside a developmental leap are a normal part of how infant health and development unfold rather than evidence that a routine has failed. The routine she had built was still there, waiting to be picked up again once the phase passed.

recent_videos.title: Sneezing After a C Section Hurts: Simple Postpartum Recovery Tips That Help
recent_videos.description:
Sneezing after a C section? Brutal. That is where this Aptaclub India Short begins, with the everyday actions nobody warns a new mother about. Coughing, laughing, sneezing and simply standing up can all pull at a healing C section wound, and for a mother who is already caring for a newborn, these small moments can be the hardest part of the first weeks of postpartum recovery.
The Short keeps the guidance practical. Move slowly, and support the tummy with a hand or a pillow when a cough, a laugh or a sneeze is coming. A comfortable feeding position can ease pressure on the abdomen, which matters because feeding happens many times a day and each session is a chance to protect the wound rather than strain it. These are small adjustments, but together they make the difference between bracing for every movement and getting through the day with less discomfort.

The other half of the message is about pace. Recovery varies, so a mother should not rush hers or measure it against anyone else's timeline. If pain is worsening rather than easing, she should call her care team instead of waiting it out, and she should keep her postnatal check, because that appointment is where recovery is properly reviewed. Postnatal recovery after a C section is a process, and listening to the body, asking for help when something feels wrong and showing up for the check are all part of maternal self-care in those first weeks.

recent_videos.title: Doctor Went Quiet During Your Pregnancy Scan? Here Is What They Are Checking
recent_videos.description:
The doctor goes quiet during a scan and a mother starts worrying. That is the moment this Aptaclub India Short is built around, and almost every expecting mother has lived it: lying on the table, watching the screen, and reading the silence in the room as a sign that something is wrong. The Short offers a simpler explanation. Sometimes, silence is just careful checking, and the quiet that feels so heavy from the table is often nothing more than a doctor concentrating.
During a pregnancy scan, the doctor is looking at the things that help understand a baby's well being: growth, heartbeat and position. Each of these takes attention, and attention often looks like quiet. More time on the screen does not always mean bad news. It can simply mean the doctor is taking the time to look properly at baby development in the womb, and that time is a sign of care rather than a cause for alarm. For a mother who has been counting the seconds of silence, that is the reframe the Short wants her to carry into her next appointment.
The other message is just as useful. Questions are always welcome, so a mother can ask what her doctor is checking instead of guessing from the silence. A short question, asked in the moment, replaces anxiety with information, and understanding the pregnancy journey brings confidence. Baby health in the womb is something a mother is allowed to understand, not only wait to hear about, and asking is how she stays part of what is happening on the screen. The silence does not change, but what it means to her does, and that is the difference between leaving a scan worried and leaving it reassured.
Aptaclub India brings doctors and parents together on exactly these questions, from pregnancy and baby health in the womb to the early days of parenting, baby immunity and everyday care. recent_videos.title: C Section Delivery Does Not Make Your Baby Weaker | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description:
This Aptaclub India Short is a doctor led explanation on one fact every mother should know: a baby born through C section delivery is not weaker because of the birth method. Many parents are told, or quietly believe, that a C section gives a baby a weaker start. The doctor explains that this is not the case. How a baby is born does not decide how strong or healthy that baby will be, and a mother who has carried this worry since the delivery deserves to hear it clearly from a paediatrician.
A C section may be planned, or it may be advised for medical reasons, and in some situations it is the safest option for both mother and baby. This is an important part of the explanation, because much of the guilt around birth and delivery comes from treating a C section as a failure rather than a medical decision. When a doctor advises a C section, it is because it is the right choice for the health of the mother and the baby at that time. A mother does not need to justify that decision, and a baby does not pay for it later.
What shapes a baby's health after birth is explained simply: feeding, hygiene, skin to skin contact, nutrition and regular paediatric checkups. These are the factors that matter in the weeks and months after a baby arrives, and each of them is as available to a C section mother as to any other. Feeding and nutrition support the baby's growth day by day. Hygiene protects the baby from everyday infection in the first months. Skin to skin contact gives warmth and closeness in the early days. Regular paediatric checkups keep infant health and development on track and pick up anything that needs attention early. None of these depend on the method of birth. For a parent thinking about baby immunity and the first year, these everyday practices are where the attention belongs, not on the birth itself.

recent_videos.title: It's Not Indigestion, It's Immunity: Cow Milk Allergy, Baby Allergies and Gut Health
recent_videos.description:
Cow milk protein allergy is not just simple indigestion. That is the correction at the heart of this Aptaclub India Short, and it matters because many parents treat the signs as a passing tummy upset. The doctor explains that cow milk protein allergy happens when a baby's immune system reacts to proteins found in cow's milk. Because it is an immune reaction rather than a digestive one, the symptoms can show up in different ways: in the gut, on the skin, and sometimes even through breathing related symptoms. For a parent trying to make sense of baby allergies, that is the first thing to understand. What looks like baby digestive problems may be the immune system at work.
The gut is important in allergy because a large part of immune activity is linked to the gut. This is why the Short connects baby allergies to gut health rather than treating them as separate topics. A baby's immune system and digestive system are developing side by side, and the balance of beneficial bacteria in the gut plays a role in how that immune system behaves. Breast milk contains HMOs, and some alternative nutrition feeds contain prebiotic oligosaccharides like GOS, FOS and HMOs. These ingredients have proven to support beneficial bacteria and hence good gut health, and good gut health leads to better immunity. For parents thinking about baby gut health and baby immunity together, this is the connection the doctor wants them to see.
The most important line in the video is the last one. If a parent suspects cow milk protein allergy, they should consult their paediatrician. Baby allergies are not something to diagnose from a video or manage on guesswork, and the gut, skin and breathing symptoms the doctor describes are reasons to seek a proper assessment rather than to wait and watch. The Short gives parents the understanding; the paediatrician gives them the plan. Knowing the difference between indigestion and an immune reaction is what gets a baby seen sooner.

recent_videos.title: Baby Said No? Try Again Later: Why Baby Food Stays in Rotation | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description: Loved it yesterday and rejected it today? Every parent who has ever spooned out a favourite baby food only to have it turned away knows the moment this Aptaclub India Short is built around. The instinct is to read it as a verdict: the child has gone off it, so it comes off the menu. This video makes the opposite case. Do not drop it from rotation. Offer it later. A food refused at one meal has not been rejected forever, it has simply been refused at that meal, and treating the two as the same thing is how a child's plate quietly shrinks over time. The guidance in the Short is practical and easy to hold on to. Pair the refused food with familiar favourites so it arrives alongside something the child already trusts. Try another texture or format, because a food that is pushed away as a mash may be accepted as a soft piece or stirred into something else. Offer variety and skip the pressure, since a child who is coaxed or pushed at the table learns to resist the plate rather than explore it. And think across meals, not moments: baby feeding is not judged by one bowl on one day, it is built over many meals, and variety in food builds nutrition over time. That last line is the heart of it. When parents zoom out from a single refused meal to the pattern of a week, feeding and nutrition start to look very different. A child who eats a narrow set of foods on Monday, tries something new on Wednesday and returns to a once refused favourite on Friday is eating a varied diet, even if no single meal looks like one. This is why the Short keeps coming back to rotation rather than removal, and to patience rather than pressure. Baby food recipes and new textures matter, but the bigger shift is in how a parent reads a refusal, and that shift is what makes variety possible in the first place. A refused bowl becomes a food to try again next week, not a food to cross off, and a child gets more chances to come round to it than a single mealtime ever allows. Over months, that is the differ

recent_videos.title: Your C Section Did Not Make Your Baby Weaker | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description: Parents of a baby born through C section delivery hear a great deal about breastfeeding, immunity, gut health and recovery, and not all of it is true. This Aptaclub India video separates facts from guilt, starting with the one every C section mother needs to hear: a baby born by C section is not weaker because of the birth method. A C section may be planned or medically necessary, and is sometimes the safest option for both. A baby's health after birth is shaped by feeding, hygiene, skin to skin contact, nutrition and regular paediatric check ups, not by how the baby arrived. Breastfeeding after a C section is possible, though the early days may need extra support while the mother recovers from surgery. Pain, tiredness and difficulty sitting comfortably can make feeding harder, which is where positioning for breastfeeding matters: the football hold or side lying can help, done safely and with guidance. If the latch is painful or the baby is not feeding well, ask for lactation support early rather than pushing through breastfeeding pain or latching issues in a newborn alone. Does a C section affect a baby's gut bacteria? A baby's gut and immune system keep developing after birth. In a vaginal birth the baby is exposed to the mother's natural bacteria, so after a C section the early gut microbiome seeding may look different. But birth is only one part of the story, and feeding and nutrition play a big role afterwards. Breast milk naturally contains prebiotic oligosaccharides like HMOs, which help feed beneficial bacteria in the baby's gut. Where a paediatrician has advised an alternate nutrition feed, parents can also discuss prebiotics like GOS and FOS if present on the pack. When prebiotics support beneficial bacteria, that interaction helps shape the gut microbiome, often described as a synbiotic effect. recent_videos.title: Her Baby Ate Four Spoons. Theirs Ate More. A Doctor on Baby Feeding and Baby Food | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description: Four spoons, and then she stopped. Is that enough? It is the question at the centre of this Aptaclub India Short, and it is one almost every parent has asked out loud, usually to another parent. In this video, a group of mothers compare notes on their children's appetites, and the comparison does exactly what comparison usually does at mealtimes: it makes the worry worse. One child eats more. Another eats a little and refuses the rest. One mother suggests trying again. Another suggests the child simply was not hungry. Every answer is well meant, and every answer leaves the mother who asked more confused than before. It is a scene most parents will recognize from their own phone. That confusion is the real subject of the video, because baby feeding is one of the few areas of parenting where every family has a number in mind and almost nobody has the same one. A friend's child finishing a full bowl of baby food does not make four spoons a failure, and a child who eats a little and pushes the rest away is not necessarily a child who is eating too little. Yet when parents measure against each other, a normal meal starts to look like a problem, and the search for a fixed amount, a baby feeding chart or a rule that settles the question once and for all begins. The answer in this Short comes from a doctor, and it is simple: every baby has their own appetite rhythm. Follow their cues rather than forcing a fixed amount. That reframe takes the number off the table. Instead of asking whether four spoons is enough, a parent learns to watch the child, to notice hunger and fullness as they show up, and to trust that a baby whose baby growth is on track and who is eating to their own rhythm is doing exactly what they should. It is advice that replaces comparison with observation, and it is the kind of reassurance that only a paediatrician, not a group chat, can really give. recent_videos.title: One Pot, Two Bowls: The Baby Food Recipe That Skips the Extra Cooking | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description: New to solids? Skip the extra cooking. That is the question, and the answer, at the heart of this Aptaclub India Short. Around six months, when a baby is ready to start solids, many parents assume that baby food means a separate pot, a separate recipe and a separate round of cooking every single day. This video shows a simpler way, using one of the most familiar dishes in an Indian kitchen: plain khichdi. The mother in this Short starts where most parents start, standing in the kitchen with the question in her head, and ends with two bowls from a single pot and a routine she can repeat tomorrow. The idea is simple enough to remember after one watch. Cook the khichdi as usual, but remove the baby's portion before the spices and salt go in. That plain portion becomes the baby's first bowl, made softer by adding a portion of milk or cream so it is gentle for a little one who is only just learning to eat. The rest of the pot gets its normal spices and salt and goes to the family. One pot of khichdi, divided into two needs, with no separate cooking at all. Same kitchen, less extra cooking. The order matters: the baby's portion comes out first, before anything is added, so the plain bowl stays plain and the family bowl stays the way the family likes it. It is the kind of small kitchen habit that saves time every day once it becomes second nature. For parents searching for baby food recipes at the start of solids, this is the kind of practical guidance that makes the transition feel manageable. The first weeks of baby feeding can be daunting, and the pressure to prepare something special for every meal adds to it. Building the baby's bowl out of the family's own khichdi keeps things simple, keeps the baby's food plain, and keeps the parent out of the kitchen for a second shift at the busiest time of the day. recent_videos.title: The Bowl He Refused Became the Bowl He Finished | Aptaclub India
recent_videos.description: Eating is learned too. Nutrition is not only on an empty plate. That is the thought this Aptaclub India Short leaves parents with, and it is one that changes how a mealtime feels. A bowl of baby food set in front of a little one is rarely eaten the way a parent hopes on the first try. It gets touched, smelled, tasted and pushed away, and to a tired parent that can look like refusal. Watched more closely, it is something else entirely. It is a child learning what food is before learning how to eat it, and every parent who has cleared a barely touched bowl will recognise the moment. That is the quiet point of this video. Baby feeding is not a single skill that arrives one day. It is built through exploring, through fingers in the bowl, through a spoon that is refused when it is offered and picked up when it is chosen. Parents often measure a meal by how much of the baby food is gone, but the plate is only half the story. The other half is what the child is learning at the table: how to hold a spoon, how to bring it to the mouth, how to decide to eat rather than be fed. A meal where very little is eaten can still be a meal where a great deal was learned, and that learning is what makes the next meal easier. For parents, the reassurance is real. When a little one pushes a bowl away, it is not a verdict on the food or on the parent. It is part of how baby feeding develops, and the patience to let a child touch, taste and try again is as much a part of good nutrition as what is in the bowl. This is why the video ends where it does: nutrition is not only about what is left on the plate, it is also about the confidence a child builds while learning to eat. Baby developmental milestones are not all about walking and talking. Learning to feed oneself is one of them, and it deserves the same patience. Technology should serve education. Not the other way around.

recent_videos.title: The Future Belongs to Kids Who Think Like Entrepreneurs | Shiv Tandan × IFT by Tata ClassEdge
recent_videos.description:
Is your child ready to build India’s next big startup? India’s Future Tycoons (IFT) by Tata ClassEdge gives students in Grades 7–12 the platform to innovate, pitch, and learn from industry leaders.

And this is exactly why through this video I wanted to introduce you to India’s Future Tycoons (IFT) by Tata ClassEdge.

IFT is an entrepreneurship competition and mentorship journey for students in Grades 7–12, where children get the opportunity to identify real-world problems, develop their own ideas, learn from founders and experts, and pitch their solutions.

🚀 Registrations are OPEN

If your child is in Grades 7–12, speak to their school about participating in India’s Future Tycoons by Tata ClassEdge.

👉 Register / Know More:
https://www.tataclassedge.com/indias-future-tycoons/

Through the IFT journey, students get:
• Entrepreneurship learning
• Founder & expert mentorship
• Opportunities to develop and pitch their ideas
• Hands-on problem-solving and innovation
• A FREE CodeAI Learning Program
• A national community of young innovators

And the top innovators can get opportunities for global exposure with NFTE, New York, networking with founders and industry leaders, and seed funding opportunities of up to ₹1 lakh.

_____________

Why am I talking about this?

Because when I say I want children to be future-ready, I don't simply mean teaching them more skills or preparing them for the next exam.

I mean giving them the confidence to spot a problem, ask questions, think differently, try something, fail, learn and try again.

That's what entrepreneurial thinking can give a child even if they never become entrepreneurs. And that’s the conversation I have with Sushil Mungekar, Founder & CEO of India’s Future Tycoons - Tata ClassEdge | Enpower Initiative, in this episode.

So watch the conversation, and then get your school involved in IFT. The next big idea could come from your child.

recent_videos.description:
Every parent has dreams for their child.
But what happens when your child starts dreaming of something completely different?

What do you think - where does guidance end and expectation begin?

recent_videos.title: What If I Mess Up My Child by Homeschooling? | Homeschooling FAQ
recent_videos.description:
What if I make the wrong decision for my child?
That fear doesn't disappear just because you choose homeschooling. Parenting itself comes with uncertainty, mistakes and plenty of ups and downs.

The goal isn't to get everything right. It's to stay resilient, stay grounded, and make sure you don't have to figure it all out alone.

Day 7 of my Homeschooling FAQ.

Have another question you're struggling with? Leave it in the comments.

recent_videos.title: Will Homeschooling Make My Child Weird & Friendless? | Homeschooling FAQ 06 | Shiv Tandan
recent_videos.description:
Won’t they become weird and friendless?

It’s one of those questions people ask about homeschooling almost as if social skills only happen at school.

But children build friendships and learn how to navigate people in far more places than a classroom.

Day 6 of my Homeschooling FAQ.

Have another question you're wondering about? Drop it in the comments.

recent_videos.title: Stop Replacing Your Child's Dreams With Your Expectations | Ft. Nikita Tomar Mann
recent_videos.description:
Sometimes, without even realising it, we start building a future for our children that looks more like our dream than theirs.

We call it guidance. We call it wanting the best for them.

But somewhere along the way, are we still listening to what they want?

A thought worth sitting with.

What do you think parents should do when a child's dream looks completely different from what they had imagined?

recent_videos.title: Can Both Parents Work Full-Time & Still Homeschool? | Homeschooling FAQ 05 | Shiv Tandan
recent_videos.description:
Maybe it's not that you're wondering whether homeschooling is possible anymore.
Maybe you're actually wondering whether it's possible for YOUR family.

"What will my child learn?
Will I be able to manage it?
What happens with Boards and college?
What if my child changes his/her mind halfway through?"

These are the questions that really matter when homeschooling stops being an idea and starts becoming a possibility.

So here's Part 2 of my Homeschooling FAQ.
And if you're still sitting with a question, ask me in the comments below.


#HomeschoolingIndia #HomeschoolingFAQ #ParentingIndia #AlternativeEducation #FixingEducation

recent_videos.description:
What we eat shapes who we become. 🌱

Join Viji and Deeraa for a complete episode 
on EATING HABITS — eating etiquettes, saying 
no to junk food, the power of Tamil millets, 
and the benefits of fruits and vegetables!

Calm. Meaningful. Bilingual. 
The Viji for Littles way. 💛

🌟 WHAT YOUR CHILD WILL LEARN:

🍽️ EATING ETIQUETTES
✅ Wash hands before eating
✅ Sit properly, eat slowly
✅ Say thank you before meals 🙏
✅ No wasting food

🚫 NO TO JUNK FOOD
✅ Too much sugar & salt — not good
✅ Chips & candy are sometimes foods
✅ Water is our everyday best friend 💧

🌾 TAMIL MILLETS
✅ கம்பு, தினை, சோளம், ராகி, வரகு
✅ Ancient Tamil superfoods 🌟
✅ Why our paatis ate millets daily
✅ Millets = Tamil cultural pride 🌾

🍎 BENEFITS OF FRUITS
✅ Natural energy and strength
✅ Rainbow fruits — every colour 
   does something special!
✅ Tamil fruits — வாழை, மாம்பழம், 
   நெல்லிக்காய், பப்பாளி!

🥦 BENEFITS OF VEGETABLES
✅ Traditional Tamil vegetables —
   முருங்கைக்காய், கத்திரிக்காய்,
   வாழைப்பூ, சேனைக்கிழங்கு!
✅ Why Amma puts drumstick 
   in the sambar! 😄

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💌 NOTE FOR PARENTS:

Tamil cuisine IS healthy food.

Idli, dosai, sambar, rasam, 
kootu, poriyal, kanji —

Our traditional Tamil food is one 
of the most nutritionally complete 
diets in the world.

This episode helps your child 
fall in love with THAT food —
the food already on your table. 💛

And teaching millets is not just 
nutrition education —
it is cultural pride. 🌾🌟

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎵 Original songs — Tamil & English
👩‍🏫 Real teacher — Viji
👧 Real child — Deeraa

recent_videos.title: No No No to Junk Food | Healthy Eating song for Kids | Viji for Littles
recent_videos.description:
No no no to junk food! 🙅‍♀️🍟

Is your little one reaching for 
chips and candy again?

Play THIS song! 😄

This fun, catchy and action-packed 
original song by Viji for Littles 
teaches children to say a big 
confident NO to junk food —
and a happy YES to healthy food! 

With head shaking, hand waving 
and crunching veggies — 
this song gets little bodies MOVING 
while teaching big life lessons! 💛

🎵 LYRICS:

No no no to junk food,
No no no not at all!
Too much sugar, too much salt,
No no no not at all!

Shake your head — no no no!
Wave your hand — go go go!
Healthy food is what we choose,
That's the way we grow grow grow!

Chips and candy — oh no!
Messy tummy — uh aw!
Fizzy drinks? No thank you please,
Water keeps us strong with ease!

No no no to junk food,
Yes yes yes to fruit! 🍎
Yes yes yes to veggies,
Crunch crunch crunch — so cute!

No no no to junk food,
No no no not at all!
Too much sugar, too much salt,
No no no not at all!

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎮 HOW TO USE THIS SONG:

This song is designed to be 
ACTIVE — not passive!

🙅 On "No no no" — 
   shake your head together!
👋 On "Go go go" — 
   wave your hand together!
🤢 On "Messy tummy uh aw" — 
   hold your tummy and make 
   a funny face! 😄
🥦 On "Crunch crunch crunch" — 
   pretend to eat a veggie 
   together!

The more dramatic the actions —
the more your child will 
REMEMBER the message! 💛

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 THE "SOMETIMES FOOD" APPROACH:

At Viji for Littles we never tell 
children that junk food is 
EVIL or SCARY.

Instead we teach —

🍟 Chips and candy are 
   SOMETIMES foods.
🍎 Fruits and vegetables are 
   EVERYDAY foods.
💧 Water is our best friend 
   every single day.

No guilt. No fear.
Just gentle, joyful understanding. 💛

This is the Montessori approach 
to food education — 
building awareness, not anxiety. 🌱

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

name: W.K. Kellogg Foundation
description:
The W.K. Kellogg Foundation (WKKF), founded in 1930 as an independent, private foundation by breakfast cereal pioneer, Will Keith Kellogg, is among the largest philanthropic foundations in the United States. Guided by the belief that all children should have an equal opportunity to thrive, WKKF works with communities to create conditions for vulnerable children so they can realize their full potential in school, work and life. 

The Kellogg Foundation is based in Battle Creek, Mich., and works throughout the United States and internationally, as well as with sovereign tribes. Special emphasis is paid to priority places where there are high concentrations of poverty and where children face significant barriers to success. WKKF priority places in the U.S. are in Michigan, Mississippi, New Mexico and New Orleans; and internationally, are in Mexico and Haiti. For more information, visit www.wkkf.org.

recent_videos.title: Professor Emily Black on Involving Employees in AI Implementation | Expanding Equity
recent_videos.description:
Who should be involved when an organization adopts AI? Responsible AI implementation depends on collaboration across an organization. Emily Black, assistant professor of Computer Science and Engineering at NYU Tandon School of Engineering and fellow at NYU School of Law, discusses why cross-functional collaboration is an important part of building a thoughtful approach to AI in the workplace.

Bringing together employees and leaders across HR, operations, legal, cybersecurity and other functions can help organizations identify potential challenges, understand how new technology will affect workers and ensure AI tools support broader organizational goals. 

Check out Expanding Equity for more strategies around building equitable and fair workplaces: expandingequity.org

recent_videos.title: Rethinking Early Childhood Education | Every Child Thrives Festival
recent_videos.description:

Peterson shared these reflections on stage at the inaugural Every Child Thrives Festival at the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago. Hosted by the W.K. Kellogg Foundation, the three-day festival brought together youth, families, educators, community advocates and artists to reimagine the future of education and community, elevate youth leadership and turn ideas into action.

Her lightning talk was part of “Imagine if We Got It Right,” a festival session that invited speakers to fast-forward 10 years and envision a future in which something has fundamentally shifted so children can truly thrive. Drawing from lived experience and professional insight, speakers shared ideas about what that future could look like and what it might take to make it possible.

recent_videos.title: Stop saying "Thank you" in English, say this instead | 20 Different Ways to Say "Thank you"
recent_videos.description:
"Thank you" is an English phrase that people use all the time. However, you might want to learn the possible variations of “thank you.” Whether you want to say this to a friend, teacher, colleague, or stranger, these creative ways to say thank you will help you improve your English conversation skills!

This video gives you 20 different ways to say "Thank You", when to use the phrase, and the tone associated with it.
-------
FAQ's:

Q: What are the different ways to express gratitude?
A: If you want to thank someone, there’s more to expressing gratitude than just saying thank you. Here’s a list of other ways to express gratitude: write a letter, give a thoughtful gift, spend quality time together, be an active listener, and offer assistance in return.

Q: What are some alternative ways to say thank you?
A: You can say the following as an alternative to thank you: appreciate it, thanks a bunch, thanks a million, thanks a ton, thanks a gazillion, thanks a load, big thanks, you rock, I owe you one.

Q: How do I reply when someone says one of these to me?
Now that you know how to say thank you, let’s also learn some ways to reply to thank you. What do you usually say when someone says “thank you” to you? If you don’t know how to answer, it can be a little bit awkward. Here’s a list of phrases you can say in return for someone’s “thank you.”

 • You’re welcome.  
 • No problem.  
 • Not a problem.  
 • No worries.  
 • My pleasure.  
 • It was nothing.  
 • Don’t worry about it.  
 • Glad I could help.  
 • Sure thing.  
 • Absolutely.

recent_videos.description:
Teachers, changing our own behavior is a roller coaster. Some days we respond calmly. Other days we fall back into old habits. All. Of. Us.

If it’s this hard for us, imagine how hard it is for our kids.
Give yourself grace. Give them grace. Keep practicing.

What behavior change has been especially challenging for you or your students? Share your experiences and strategies in the comments.
#teachers #teachersofinstagram

recent_videos.title: 2nd To Last Word is Best  #educator
recent_videos.description:
When a student pushes back, our instinct is often to respond, correct, or make sure we have the final say. But sometimes the most powerful move is knowing when not to engage.

Give them the second-to-last word. Then move on.

It’s not about “winning” the interaction—it’s about protecting the relationship, keeping control of the situation, and getting back to what really matters.

Now, I am not saying that you don't go back at another time and address the comments privately.  I believe you should.  However, in the moment if you want defuse the situation and move on, this strategy works well!

Teachers: How do you avoid getting pulled into power struggles with students? Drop your best strategy in the comments.

#Relationships1st #ConnectionBeforeCorrection #Teachers #ClassroomManagement #TeacherTips #Education #StudentEngagement #TeachingStrategies

recent_videos.title: First Time I Felt Good About School
recent_videos.description:
I will never forget when my English teacher allowed me to get up in front of the class and tell a few jokes.  I was good at public speaking, which normally got me in trouble in school because it wasn't always at the right times. 

However, on this particular day, I stood up there proudly, told a couple of jokes, got some laughs, and got complimented by my teacher.  He gave me my start to what I am doing today!  And it wasn't in the curriculum!
#teachers #educator

recent_videos.title: What is causing teacher burnout  #classroomenvironment
recent_videos.description:
Teachers are being torn apart with the constant push to hit the curriculum milestones laid out by state education officials. Meanwhile, the kids are showing up without basic social skills, which need to be taught as well so their classroom can function smoothly. So teachers get pulled in both directions, what they are supposed to teach and what their students need to learn often don't line up and that can be exhausting! 

My advice is to give your students what they need and trust that by doing so, it will lead you back to what they are supposed to learn.   
#teachers

recent_videos.title: How Well Do Your Students KnowYou   #classroomenvironment #education
recent_videos.description:
Relationship building is a two way street. I learn something about you and you learn something about me. And letting kids know your struggles and challenges as well as your successes is what helps build the strong relationships with your students.
#classroommanagement

recent_videos.description:

recent_videos.title: High-Risk Double Marker Test? | Dr. Pavana N | Motherhood Hospitals, Indiranagar
recent_videos.description:
What does a high-risk Double Marker Test result mean during pregnancy? Does it confirm a chromosomal condition in the baby?

In this video, Dr. Pavana N explains the purpose of the Double Marker Test, a prenatal screening test that assesses the likelihood of certain chromosomal conditions.

She discusses how the test considers markers such as free beta-hCG and PAPP-A alongside maternal factors and NT scan findings. A high-risk result does not automatically confirm a problem with the pregnancy.

Dr. Pavana also explains why further evaluation may be recommended, including Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT), which is another screening test rather than a diagnostic test.

Watch the video to understand prenatal screening results and why discussing the next steps with your doctor is important.

recent_videos.title: What Happens to Your Body After a C-Section? | Motherhood Hospitals
recent_videos.description:
Recovery after a C-section involves more than incision healing. Your body is also adjusting to hormonal changes, breastfeeding, disrupted sleep and the physical demands of caring for your newborn.

What Changes Can You Expect?
- Hormonal shifts may affect mood, energy and appetite
- Incision pain, tenderness or tightness can occur
- Breast fullness and changes in milk production are common
- Fatigue is expected as your body recovers

How Can You Support Your Recovery?
- Keep your incision clean and dry as advised
- Begin gentle movement when your doctor recommends it
- Prioritise nutritious meals, hydration and rest
- Find comfortable breastfeeding positions that support your incision

Know When to Seek Medical Advice:
Every C-section recovery is different. Contact your doctor if you experience fever, increasing pain, wound redness or discharge, or heavy bleeding. Give your body time to heal and seek support when you need it.

recent_videos.title: Is Your “Period Pain” Really Just Period Pain? | Motherhood Hospitals
recent_videos.description:
Period pain is common, but severe, recurring or worsening pelvic pain should not be dismissed as normal. Conditions such as endometriosis, fibroids and ovarian cysts can cause symptoms that affect everyday life.

What Could Be Causing Your Pelvic Pain?
✅ Endometriosis may cause worsening period pain and pain between periods
✅ Fibroids can be associated with heavy bleeding and pelvic pressure
✅ Ovarian cysts may cause one-sided pain, bloating or discomfort
✅ Pain during intercourse or bowel movements may need evaluation
When Should You Seek Medical Advice?
✅ Pain that is severe, recurring or getting worse
✅ Period pain that interferes with daily activities
✅ Unusually heavy or irregular menstrual bleeding
✅ Pelvic pain that occurs outside your period

Don't Normalise Persistent Pelvic Pain:
A gynaecological evaluation can help identify the underlying cause and guide appropriate care. Sudden, severe pelvic pain needs urgent medical attention.

recent_videos.title: 10 AI Commands to Make Studying Easier! 🎓🤖
recent_videos.description:
AI is changing the way we learn, but most students still use it in the simplest way possible — asking questions and getting answers. What if you could use AI to do much more than that?

What if a simple command could turn a difficult topic into a visual explanation, organize an entire chapter into a mind map, transform information into an infographic, create a timeline, build a 3D model, break down a complex object with an exploded view, or even turn a topic into something more engaging and easier to remember?

That’s exactly what we’re exploring in this video.

I’ve put together 10 useful AI commands that can genuinely help students with their studies. And this isn’t going to be another video where I simply show you a list of commands and tell you what they supposedly do. name: Prachis Phonics Class
description:
Phonics learning is crucial for children because it provides a systematic foundation for reading, writing, and spelling by teaching them the connection between letters and sounds. 

Our Key features include:
Systematic and Structured Curriculum: Lessons follow a clear, step-by-step progression, starting with basic letter sounds and moving to more complex combinations, ensuring a logical learning sequence.

Focus on Letter-Sound Correspondence: Children learn the specific sound (phoneme) that each letter or group of letters (grapheme) makes, rather than just the alphabet names.

Blending and Segmenting Skills: A core component is teaching children how to blend individual sounds together to form words (e.g., c-a-t makes "cat" for reading) and how to segment words into their individual sounds for spelling.

Decoding Unfamiliar Words: Children are given the tools to sound out new or tricky words independently, building their confidence and self-reliance in reading.
