recent_videos.title: How Gilman School Uses Data to Drive Real Change
recent_videos.description:
In this episode, Cindy Blackburn sits down with Rachel Gorsky, Director of Institutional Research and Data Analytics at Gilman School, to explore how schools can actually use data to drive meaningful change.

They unpack what institutional research looks like in K–12 independent schools, how to move from vague questions to actionable insights, and why combining qualitative and quantitative data is essential for understanding school culture.

Rachel shares her process for analyzing school climate surveys, navigating sensitive topics, and turning complex data into findings that leaders can actually use. The conversation also dives into a real research project on women’s experiences in boys’ schools, offering a powerful example of how data can surface hidden patterns and inform leadership decisions.

They also explore the ethical challenges of working with sensitive data, how to build trust through transparency, and why sharing findings is often the hardest part of the process.
If you're a school leader, educator, or anyone interested in data-informed decision-making in education, this episode offers practical insights you can apply right away.

recent_videos.title: Building AI literacy in schools, lessons from Pingry School
recent_videos.description:
On this episode of the School Leaders Project, host Cindy Blackburn sits down with Dr. Danielle Mirliss, Director of Research and Academic Innovation at Pingry School, to explore how schools can build AI literacy with purpose, ethics, and trust.

Danielle shares how Pingry has shifted from creating rigid AI policies to grounding its approach in clear values, keeping relationships, critical thinking, and student agency at the center of teaching and learning. Together, they unpack what families are most concerned about when it comes to artificial intelligence in schools, from academic integrity and misinformation to the future of education and work.

The conversation dives into practical strategies for supporting teachers, engaging parents, and developing an AI literacy curriculum that helps students understand how AI works, how to use it responsibly, and how to think critically about its ethical impact.

If you’re a school leader, educator, or parent looking for a thoughtful, real-world approach to teaching AI in K–12 schools, this episode offers clarity, reassurance, and actionable ideas.

recent_videos.title: How Aurora Public Schools is rethinking equity, AI, and instruction
recent_videos.description:
On this episode of the School Leaders Project, host Cindy Blackburn sits down with Antonio Vigil, Director of Innovative Classroom Technology at Aurora Public Schools, to explore what it really takes to transform public education in a moment of rapid change.

Together, they unpack how Aurora Public Schools is rethinking equity, AI, and instruction through its districtwide strategy, Destination APS. Antonio shares powerful stories of using AI to support multilingual learners, build belonging through real-time translation, and strengthen relationships between schools and families.

The conversation dives into the “both and” philosophy of education: creating rigorous, engaging learning experiences while also centering relationships, empathy, and student voice. You’ll hear practical insights on data literacy, dashboards for educators, street data for equity, liberatory design, and why adaptive leadership matters when schools are moving beyond improving the status quo.

If you’re a school leader, educator, or anyone interested in the future of teaching and learning, this episode offers a hopeful, grounded look at how systems can change in meaningful ways.

recent_videos.description:
Is your child constantly glued to their smartphone? 📱

In today's digital age, kids have the world at their fingertips—from YouTube to AI tools like ChatGPT. While this means instant access to information without needing to ask parents, it also brings major distractions, endless scrolling, and exposure to misinformation or inappropriate content.

Technology has changed, but has your parenting? Here are 3 essential hacks to manage your child's digital habits:

✔️ **Don't Make the Phone an Enemy:** Instead of fighting it, set clear family rules and boundaries regarding screen time and allowed apps.
✔️ **Control the Content, Not Just the Clock:** 30 minutes of an educational video is completely different from 30 minutes of mindless scrolling. Ensure they are engaging with curious, educational, or age-appropriate entertainment.
✔️ **Get Involved:** Talk to them about their online world. Ask them to teach you what they learned on YouTube or AI that day to build better interaction.

Parenting around technology is no longer just about controlling it; it's about guiding your child.

recent_videos.title: 90% of your child’s brain develops before age 7—are you giving them your time or just a screen?
recent_videos.description:
What is the most important phase in your child's life? 

Many parents assume it's during their 10th standard, 12th standard, or college years. But research tells a completely different story. The most critical period for shaping a human being is actually from birth to 7 years old.   In this insightful episode of Parenting Hacks with Meghna, we explore why early childhood is the foundation for your child's entire future. During the first 7 years, 90% of a child’s brain development occurs. Their brain acts like a sponge, absorbing everything they see, hear, and experience.  

 Key Takeaways from this session:

Observation Over Lectures: Children in this phase do not learn from lectures; they learn by observing your behavior. If they see respect and patience at home, they adopt it; if they see shouting, they normalize it.   

Time Over Material Gifts: Expensive toys, gadgets, and AC rooms do not guarantee a successful life. Your child craves your undivided attention, deep conversations, and active playtime.  
 
Crucial Skill Building: Outdoor play naturally develops problem-solving skills, while listening to stories builds language and communication abilities.   

Common Mistakes to Avoid: Stop handing them a phone the moment they cry, reducing conversation time because you are busy, and comparing them to other children.   

The 20-Minute Rule: Dedicate at least 20 minutes daily to distraction-free playtime, reading books, pretending, and building an emotional connection with your child.   

These first 7 years won't dictate if your child becomes a doctor or an engineer, but they will decide if they become a confident, kind, and emotionally strong adult. You don't need to provide a perfect environment—just a caring and loving one.

recent_videos.title: Why Parents Always Say "NO" (It’s Not What You Think!) | Parenting Hacks with Meghna
recent_videos.description:
"I don't do anything wrong, but my parents still don't trust me!" 🥺
 Sound familiar? 

  We’ve all been there, fighting for that one permission to go out with friends. But here is a reality check from today's session: That constant "NO" from your parents usually isn’t about a lack of trust. It’s actually about fear. 💡

Parents often operate from a place of intense protection. When they imagine you stepping out, their minds immediately rush to, "What if something goes wrong?" or "What if they get hurt?" They aren't trying to ruin your social life—they are just terrified for your safety. But because they only express that anxiety as a strict "NO," it just feels like rejection and distrust to you.  

 It’s time to bridge this communication gap. Teens, understanding the emotion behind the "No" is your first step. Parents, expressing your fears instead of just laying down rules can change everything.  

 Share this with your parents or your teenager, and let's start a real conversation! 👇

 Let us know in the comments: do you struggle with this in your house?

recent_videos.description:
What started as a little getaway turned into one of the most beautiful and memorable trips! ❤️ From colourful streets and historic forts to peaceful beaches, beautiful nights and a luxurious tent stay — Daman definitely has so much more to offer than I expected!

In this vlog, come along with me as we explore the beautiful sides of Daman! ✨

We stayed at 📍The Fern Seaside Luxurious Tent Resort, Moti Daman Fort 🌴✨ The property offers a unique luxury-tent experience and is close to several major heritage attractions. The resort features premium tent-style accommodation, an outdoor pool, dining options, a bar and spa facilities, making it a great choice if you're looking for a relaxing and luxurious stay experience. 

🌈 Colourful Streets of Moti Daman

Bom Jesus  church 💒
Daman Lighthouse Dominican Monastery
🏖️ Devka Beach & Jampore Beach🏖
🏰 Nani Daman Fort / St. Jerome Fort
 Weekend Getaways 🌴 | Staycations ✨

💡 QUICK TRAVEL TIP

Daman is compact enough to explore over a weekend. I would recommend grouping Moti Daman's heritage attractions together, while keeping Devka Beach and Nani Daman for a relaxed evening. That way, you're not constantly travelling back and forth across town.

 Looking Older Than Your Actual Age? These 5 Everyday Factors May Be Affecting Your Appearance!

In this video, discover 5 possible factors that may contribute to premature skin aging and learn how to support healthier-looking skin.

 5 Factors That May Make You Look Older:

Too Much Sun Exposure ☀️ – UV rays can damage skin and contribute to wrinkles and dark spots.

Poor Sleep Habits 😴 – Inadequate sleep may affect your skin's appearance and overall well-being.

Unhealthy Eating Habits 🥗 – A balanced diet supports healthy skin and general health.

Not Drinking Enough Water 💧 – Dehydration can make fine lines appear more noticeable temporarily.

Chronic Stress 🧠 – Long-term stress may affect skin health and overall wellness.

💡 Simple Tips for Healthy-Looking Skin:
✅ Use sunscreen regularly.
✅ Maintain a consistent sleep schedule.
✅ Eat a balanced, nutritious diet.
✅ Drink enough water throughout the day.
✅ Find healthy ways to manage stress.

Remember, aging is a natural process, and everyone ages differently. Small, healthy lifestyle changes can support your overall well-being.

recent_videos.description:
Kya aap jaante hain ki betiyaan bhi apni maternal genetic lineage ko generation after generation aage badhati hain? 🧬

Science ke according, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) aam taur par maa se bachchon ko milta hai. Lekin ise agli generation tak generally sirf maternal line—yaani beti, uski beti aur phir uski beti—ke through pass kiya jaata hai.

Iska matlab ye nahi ki bete apni genetic lineage aage nahi badhate. Nuclear DNA ke through bete aur betiyaan dono apne genes agli generation tak pass karte hain.

Is video mein samjhiye mitochondrial DNA ka role aur kyun betiyon ko kam samajhna scientific facts ke khilaaf hai.

Say NO to female foeticide. Every child deserves equal love and respect. 💙

recent_videos.description:
⚠️ Are old roofing sheets a hidden health risk?

Some roofing sheets contain asbestos, a mineral that can release microscopic fibres into the air when damaged or disturbed.

Inhaling asbestos fibres can increase the risk of serious diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma. These diseases may take decades to develop.

🚫 Never cut, break, or remove suspected asbestos sheets yourself.

✅ Consult trained professionals for assessment and safe removal.

recent_videos.title: Can You Change Your Baby's Skin Color? 🥥 #pregnancynutrition #babydevelopment #pregnancytips
recent_videos.description:
Does drinking coconut water during pregnancy make your baby fair or white? 🤰🥥

No — this is a myth. ❌

Coconut water can be a refreshing source of hydration during pregnancy, but it cannot change your baby’s natural skin colour.

Your baby’s skin colour is mainly influenced by genetics and melanin, with genetic factors inherited from both parents.

Milk, kesar, coconut water, or specific fruits cannot make a baby fair.

The real goal of pregnancy nutrition is healthy growth and development, not changing your baby’s skin colour. ❤️

recent_videos.title: How to Answer Your Boss Confidently | Communication Skills #shorts #awards #interview
recent_videos.description:
How to answer your boss confidently, stop rambling, and speak clearly when you’re put on the spot in meetings, interviews or presentations.

Most professionals don’t struggle because of English. They struggle because of structure. When your boss asks a simple question, your brain is trying to form an opinion, organize thoughts, choose words, and monitor how you’re coming across, all at the same time.

In this short, Sanjeev Datta shares a simple 4-step framework to answer any question with clarity:

✅ ANSWER: Start with your answer first. “Yes, I think we should delay it by a week.”
✅ REASON: Give one clear reason. “The current version still has two issues that could affect customer experience.”
✅ EXAMPLE: Back it with one piece of evidence. “We’re still seeing failures at the payment stage.”
✅ STOP: Stop talking. Don’t ruin a good answer by over-explaining.

And if you need 2 seconds before answering, take them. Pausing looks confident. Rambling doesn’t.

✅ ANSWER only that part: Solve the one objection that’s actually stopping them from agreeing.

recent_videos.title: Autism & Wrong Answers #autismparenting#autismspeech#executive functioning
recent_videos.description:
Paraphasia (word substitutions) in autistic children 🧠

What it looks like: your child says “pencil” for pen, “sit” for chair, “dog” for cat. A related word comes out in place of the exact word.

Why it happens: the brain stores words in networks. When your child sees a pen, related words come up with it: pencil, write, paper, school. Executive functioning then selects the one that fits the situation. Many autistic children and children with ADHD find this selection step difficult. They know the word, but a related one comes out.

What you can do

1. Avoid saying “wrong.” Model the correct word naturally. Child: “pencil.” You: “Yes, a pen. We write with a pen.”
2. Offer a choice of two. “Do you want water or juice?”
3. Give time for processing. Pause and let your child retrieve the word before you step in.
4. Notice the connection your child made. It tells you how their language network is organised.
5. Work on executive functioning skills: daily routines, visual schedules, sorting objects into categories, games where they choose between options, and “what else can we call this?” play.
#autisticspeech #autismparenting #speechtherapy #autismindia #executivefunctioning

recent_videos.title: 3 Silly Speech Games | Autism, Apraxia & Gestalt Learners
recent_videos.description:
ACTIVITY SHEET ⬇️
1️⃣. Temperature Play (Cold Spoon, Warm Spoon)
Keep two spoons ready, one in the fridge and one in a cup of warm (never hot) water. The parent touches them to the child’s hand, cheek, tummy, or toes, and the child reacts. Then make it a guessing game: the child closes their eyes and decides whether it’s cold or warm before the spoon lands, then predicts where it’s going next. Swapping roles is the best part, because the child gets to tickle the parent.

Goals
1 : “brrr,” “cold,” “hot/warm,” “again,” “more,” plus body-part words (hand, toe, nose).
2: “Cold spoon on my tummy,” “I want warm spoon.”
3: predicting and explaining (“I think it’s cold because it was in the fridge”), comparing (“The cold one is tickly, the warm one is cozy”).
4. Apraxia: "hisss" “brrr” is a lovely lip-and-voice sound, easy to imitate, and the dramatic reaction gives lots of natural repetitions.

Caveat: use the fridge, not the freezer, because frozen steel can stick to skin. Test the warm one on your own wrist first. Some autistic children are touch-sensitive, so start on their hand and let them control where it goes.

2️⃣ Silly Spoon Mistakes
The parent “feeds” a stuffed toy, but gets it wrong on purpose. A shoe on the spoon, a crayon, a toy car. The child’s job is to catch the mistake and fix it. Kids absolutely love correcting adults, and it creates real reasons to speak. Kids find it funny when you say "yucky" and 'spit' it far away too. 

Goals
1: “no!”, “yuck,” “shoe,” “eat,” “stop.”
2: “No, not shoe!”, “Bear wants rice,” “That’s not food.”
3: reasoning and categories (“We can’t eat a shoe because it isn’t food,” “What does the bear really like?”).
4: Apraxia: “no” and “uh-oh” give huge payoff for easy sounds, and the humor keeps repetition from feeling like drill.

3️⃣. Big Spoon, Tiny Spoon Voices
Use a ladle or big serving spoon and a tiny teaspoon as “microphones.” Speaking into the big one means a big, loud, deep voice, like a giant. The tiny one means a squeaky,

Use your clinical judgment. 👩‍🔬

Documenting support areas is important. Needing deficit information to avail school support and health services is important. But assessment can be more than just that.

For example:

👶 Parent: “He isn’t talking yet.”
Instead of “When was his first word? When did he combine two words?” — find out what he understands, how he communicates without words, what he can imitate, what’s the sound repertoire.

👧 Parent: “She doesn’t interact with other children.”
Instead of “Does she take turns? Does she share? Does she initiate?” — first understand what social communication currently looks like for her. Does she notice people? Share enjoyment? Respond when someone joins her? What happens during play?

recent_videos.title: Is Autism Genetic? #autism #autismmom
recent_videos.description:
1️⃣ What can actually cause autism?

• Genetic factors — the biggest contributor to autism
• Rubella infection during pregnancy — can cause congenital rubella syndrome, which is linked with autism
• Valproate exposure during pregnancy — linked with autism

Autism is complex and there is usually no single cause we can point to.

2️⃣ What can increase the chance of autism?

• Having an autistic sibling
• Older parental age
• Prematurity
• Low birth weight
• Severe birth complications
• Maternal diabetes during pregnancy
• Some prenatal exposure to air pollution or heavy metals
• Some medicines taken during pregnancy

These factors may contribute, but they do not explain autism in every child. (World Health Organization)

3️⃣ What does NOT cause autism?

❌ Vaccines
❌ Screen time
❌ Parenting
❌ Bad parenting
❌ A lack of affection
❌ Diet
❌ Sugar
❌ Something the child did after birth
❌ A mother’s emotional stress during pregnancy

#AutismIsGenetic #GeneticTesting #AutismDiagnosis #SpeechTherapy #Genetics

recent_videos.title: What we see on the outside is language — words, sentences, questions, answers.
recent_videos.description:
What we see on the outside is language — words, sentences, questions, answers.

But underneath every conversation, there is a lot happening.

A child may need to:

→ Pay attention to what the other person is saying
→ Hold information in working memory while thinking about an answer
→ Understand the question and work out what information is being asked for
→ Find the right words to express an idea
→ Plan and organise those words into a sentence
→ Think about another person’s perspective
→ Solve a problem when communication breaks down
→ Use emotional language to understand and explain how they feel
→ Be flexible when the conversation doesn’t go the way they expected

This is why a child can know the words but still struggle to use them in conversation.

And this is also why we don’t teach all of this by simply asking more questions.

At home, you can support these skills by:

→ Use multiple ways to teach: say it, show it, act it out, use a picture, and let your child experience it.

→ Reduce the memory load: instead of giving 3 instructions at once, give one step, let them do it, then add the next.

→ Give thinking time: ask a question and wait. Don’t immediately repeat it or give the answer.

→ Model the language you want: instead of asking, “Why are you upset?”, model, “You’re upset because the game ended.”

→ Talk through problems together: “The tower fell. Hmm… what can we do now?”

→ Teach language for real situations: “I don’t like that,” “Help me,” “I need a break,” “What happened?” “What should we do?”

→ Talk about thoughts and feelings during everyday life: “I thought it would rain, but it didn’t.” “I think she’s upset because her toy broke.”

The goal isn’t just more language.

It’s helping your child use language to think, solve problems, understand people and share their world.

recent_videos.title: How to support play and why they matter 👇
recent_videos.description:
How to support play and why they matter 👇

🧩 Solo play
• Helps children regulate and recharge.
• Builds attention and independent problem-solving.
• Gives you clues about their interests—your best starting point for language.

👫 Parallel play (playing beside your child without taking over)
• Reduces pressure to interact.
• Helps your child become comfortable sharing space with another person.
• A perfect opportunity to model language naturally without expecting a response.

🤝 Interactive play
• Builds turn-taking, shared attention and flexibility.
• Teaches children that communication changes what happens next.
• Keep it playful, not performance-based.

🏃 Movement play
• Jumping, swinging, climbing, chasing…
• Helps many autistic and ADHD children regulate their bodies before they’re ready to engage.
• Regulation is often the first step to communication.

🎭 Pretend play
• Builds imagination, flexible thinking and understanding different perspectives.
• Creates natural opportunities for rich language.
• It develops differently for every child, so don’t rush it.

💡 A few play shifts that make a big difference
• Follow your child’s interests before introducing your own ideas.
• Ovserve their play before trying to teach.
• Comment more than you question.
• Aim to make your child laugh more than you aim to make them talk.

You don’t have to stop playing to start teaching.

Play is already teaching. The goal is to recognise those opportunities and learn how to build communication through them, not instead of them.

recent_videos.title: Parents are often told, “Talk to your child more.”
recent_videos.description:
Parents are often told, “Talk to your child more.”

So they do this:

“What’s this?”
“What colour is it?”
“Who is that?”
“What did you eat?”
“What’s the animal’s name?”

But here’s what I notice in therapy.

Sometimes I’ll watch a parent interact with their child for five minutes…
…and they’ve asked 40 questions.

Do you know how many complete language models the child heard?

Maybe five.

Every question is a missed opportunity to give language instead of asking for language.

For example…

Instead of:
❌ “What did you eat at school?”

Try:
✅ “I wonder if you had rice today. I packed your lunch, I put lots of yummy mango in it.”

Now your child hears:

* wonder
* today
* packed
* lunch
* yummy
* mango

One question became five or six new language models.

Instead of:
❌ “What colour is your car?”

Try:
✅ “Your tiny blue car is driving so fast! Oh no… it crashed!”

Instead of:
❌ “Where’s the ball?”

Try:
✅ “The ball rolled under the sofa. Let’s look together.”

Instead of:
❌ “What are you drawing?”

Try:
✅ “You’re drawing a huge dinosaur! It has such a long tail.”

Here’s the shift I want parents to make:

When your child already knows the answer…
…don’t ask.

Tell. Describe. Wonder. Predict. React.

Because children can’t learn language they don’t hear.

And if most of your talking is asking questions…
…your child is hearing far less language than you think.

How is Computational Thinking (CT) shaping the future of education? Why has CBSE brought Computational Thinking and Artificial Intelligence together, and what does this mean for teachers, students, and schools?

Welcome to the Super Mind Show, where we explore the ideas transforming education and learning.

In this episode, Manmohan speaks with Bhanu Prasad, Founder & CEO of Super Teacher Edureforms Pvt. Ltd., a Hyderabad-based STEM education solutions provider, to understand the importance of Computational Thinking (CT), its connection with Mathematics, and how schools can integrate it into everyday teaching and learning.

In this episode, we discuss:

00:00 - Intro,
01:03 What is Computational Thinking, and why does it matter today?,
03:50 Why is CT relevant in the age of Artificial Intelligence?,
09:17 What changes can teachers and schools expect from the CBSE CT & AI initiative?
10:35 How can we explain CT to someone without a technical background?
15:35 Real-life examples of Computational Thinking in students' everyday learning.
19:10 Why did Computational Thinking naturally begin with Mathematics?
21:32 Where do we CT and AI placed ?
22:58 Why did CT naturally start with Mathematics?  
27:27 What are radical and systematic changes you want to bring to today's education. 
32:40 What is your say on the CT teacher responsibility or accountability once it gets embedded with all the core subjects ?   

A conversation for every educator

Whether you are a school leader, teacher, education professional, or parent, this episode offers perspectives on preparing students for a future where thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and AI literacy matter.

Guest: Bhanu Prasad
Founder & CEO, Super Teacher Edureforms Pvt. Ltd.

recent_videos.title: Everything I Wish Women Knew About Fertility | Dr. Natalie Crawford
recent_videos.description:
This week on Certified Oversharer, I’m joined by Natalie Crawford, MD — a double board-certified fertility doctor, author of The Fertility Formula, and host of the As a Woman Podcast with over 5 million downloads. Dr. Crawford takes a whole-body approach to fertility, combining lifestyle and functional medicine with science-backed facts to help women better understand their bodies and advocate for themselves. She’s helped thousands of patients and followers navigate their fertility journeys with clarity, education, and empowerment.

In this episode, we get real about infertility — and challenge a lot of what women have been told. From why “waiting a year” might not always be the best advice, to how inflammation, stress, and everyday toxins could be impacting your fertility, Dr. Crawford breaks it all down in a way that actually makes sense. We talk about the small lifestyle changes you can start making today, including what to cut out, how chronic stress affects your hormones, and practical ways to feel more in control during the process.

We also dive into the realities of fertility treatment — including whether IVF is being pushed too soon, why “unexplained infertility” might not be so unexplained, and the importance of understanding the why behind your diagnosis. Dr. Crawford shares insight on supplements that are actually worth it (and which ones can do more harm than good), the role of peptides and GLP-1s, and clears up major myths around birth control, hormone testing, and what regular cycles really mean for your chances of getting pregnant.

If you’ve ever felt confused, frustrated, or overwhelmed trying to understand your fertility — this episode is for you. Because infertility isn’t just a diagnosis… It’s often a symptom, and you deserve to know what your body is trying to tell you.

recent_videos.title: The Best Preschool Curriculum Isn't a Curriculum
recent_videos.description:
The best preschool curriculum isn't something you buy. 👇

Think of your toddler as your apprentice.
🍳 In the kitchen? Get them in the kitchen.
🥕 Chopping vegetables? Let them chop.
⛽ Getting gas? Let them help fill the tank.

Then talk them through it: what you're doing, and WHY.

👀 Let them see it ✋ Let them touch it 👂 Let them hear it ❓ Welcome every "why?"

That's how kids build the vocabulary that sets them apart. Most kids just aren't spoken to.

It's not a preschool curriculum. It's a LIFE curriculum. And the best person to teach it is the one they spend all day with: you.

Want help building this into your days?
Comment HOMESCHOOL and let's chat.

recent_videos.title: Doing everything for your kids isn't good for them or you
recent_videos.description:
Piano, parkour, chemistry, art and a museum trip, all fighting for the same three afternoons.

Every one was genuinely good. That was the problem.

She wasn’t protecting her kids’ opportunities by refusing to cut anything. She was protecting herself from the guilt of being the mom who said no.

So we ran every activity through her family’s Foundation, the three things they said matter most. Two stayed. Three left.

Try it on your own calendar. For each activity, ask:

Does it serve one of our top three priorities?
Would we sign up for it again today?
What does it cost us in time, money and margin?

If an activity fails two of the three, it goes.

Every change is an exchange, never just an addition.

Can’t name your three priorities? That’s the real problem, and it’s where I start with every family. Comment MAP and my team will help you build yours.

#homeschool #homeschoolmom #homeschoolschedule #homeschoollife #christianhomeschool

recent_videos.title: Why I’m Getting My FSH Checked Again Before 40
recent_videos.description:
Apparently, early menopause was part of my family history.  Thankfully, we were successful in our third round of IVF and had our twins!

I wish we talked more openly about this stuff. Not just whether we want children, but what our mothers and grandmothers experienced and what questions we might want to ask about our own health.

As I approach 40, I’m revisiting something I never fully understood a decade ago. I don’t have that answer yet, but I’m getting checked instead of continuing to guess.

NOTE: 

1. Having kids at 20 doesn't guarantee avoiding ovarian insufficiency, that was more a comment on the fact that we probably would have started trying sooner.

2. Most docs won't actually run bloodwork on your FSH when you come in with perimenopause symptoms. The reason we're getting it looked at is that my FSH was already so high in my early 20's, so it would be good to see where it's at now.

3. FSH of 23 alone doesn't establish menopause.

Follow along while I figure out my next chapter!

#WomensHealth #EarlyMenopause #HormoneHealth #InfertilityJourney

recent_videos.title: My Identical Twins Disagree About the Flu Shot
recent_videos.description:
Same DNA, very different opinions. That pretty much sums up parenting identical twins (iykyk).

This year’s flu shot conversation at the doctor's office reminded me how independently my girls think, and how much I’m still figuring out about giving them a voice in decisions as they grow.

I’m curious how our flu season will unfold.  In reality, one season with one set of twins won’t tell us whether a vaccine works, and a symptom showing up afterward doesn’t tell me what caused it. I’m just here sharing our experience, with plenty still to learn!

How do you give your kids room to speak up at doctor’s appointments? And fellow twin parents: what do yours have completely opposite opinions about?

#TwinParenting #IdenticalTwins #Parenting #FluSeason

recent_videos.title: I Gave My Dogs Treats. They Followed Me for Two Hours.
recent_videos.description:
Mark is the treat parent. I’m the “you’ve been fed and walked, please respect my personal space” parent.

I know dog treats are useful, especially for training. It’s the bossy little treat committee that forms around me afterward that brings out my need for control. Not saying that's a good thing; just being honest that I'm a LITTLE OCD sometimes...

But the girls wanted to spoil the dogs, and sometimes I can let a little joy outrank my need to manage absolutely everything.

The girls were delighted. The hounds were delighted. I spent the next two hours saying, “Go away" to the dogs who kept looking at me with those BEGGIN' EYES (you know the ones).

Worth it. Begrudgingly.

These @boccesbakery treats were gifted to us before our farmhouse move and resurfaced during unpacking. I’ve lost track of who originally sent them, but thank you for a very happy morning for my girls and dogs.

Who’s the treat dispenser in your house?

#DogMomLife #DogTreats #LifeWithDogs #PrettySweetAcres

Lake Junaluska is my kind of fall outing in Western North Carolina: easy to enjoy with kids and dogs, and pretty enough to make me put my phone away. After getting a few clips, obviously.

recent_videos.title: The Homeschooling Freedom I Appreciate Most
recent_videos.description:
One of my favorite things about homeschooling is having a say in how we spend our days.

I want my girls to have time for friendships, to be outside, and to try things just because they’re curious. I also want to give their lessons the attention they deserve. Having a flexible homeschool schedule gives me room for all of that, without everything needing to happen in a particular order.

Some days, sitting down with our books comes later. That doesn’t mean the learning waited until we got home.

If you homeschool, what’s the freedom you appreciate most? If you’re considering it, what would you love to have more time for?

#Homeschooling #HomeschoolLife #HomeschoolMom #LearningThroughLife

recent_videos.title: and what animal should we get next?
recent_videos.description:
I think restoring an old farmhouse involves two kinds of decisions: what color to paint the porch and what farm animal to bring home next.

I want to keep as much of our farmhouse’s original character as possible. The original porch railing was white, so that’s where I’m leaning. Would you do white railings with a stained porch floor, or another combination?

Then there’s the animal question. I love the idea of adding to our little farm, but for full context, unless it's a bird (turkey/chicken), it'll be a pet. We also aren't home every day so it would have to be relatively low maintenance (particularly when it comes to socialization). Sheep? A pig? A cow? A pony? A FRIGGIN YAK!? 

#PrettySweetAcres #HistoricFarmhouse #FarmLife #FrontPorch

recent_videos.title: We Read the Difficulty Sign AFTER the Hike (Van Cliff Loop)
recent_videos.description:
Apparently I’m becoming a hiking person.

I’ve been taking the girls to explore a trail every Monday, and somewhere along the way I stopped wishing we’d just gone for a flat, easy walk. Now I’m curious about what we’ll find next. Watching them tackle something hard makes me want to keep going, too.

Van Cliff Loop near Hot Springs, NC, gave us 3.3 miles and 948 feet of elevation gain from our starting point at Rocky Bluff Campground. I would have appreciated reading the “most difficult” sign BEFORE we finished, but I’m pretty pleased with us. I also got hangry half way through so snacks are a must next time.

#HikingWithKids #WNCHiking #FamilyAdventures #HikingWithDogs

recent_videos.title: Our First Homeschool Baking Day—Would Every Kid Find a Job?
recent_videos.description:
I am starting to realize that I need to give my kids a little more room to show me what they can do. It’s easy to default to “I’ll do that part” when we’re cooking together, especially when I want to get dinner on the table.

That’s one thing I loved about this homeschool baking day: we had time to let them try. I came home wanting to make more room for that in our own kitchen.

I also came home wanting a full canning pantry and a wheat mill, so these homeschool outings could get expensive.

What’s a recipe your kids love helping with? I’m collecting ideas for my turn to host. Bonus points if there are jobs for different ages.

\#HomeschoolLife #BakingWithKids #HandsOnLearning #Homesteading

recent_videos.title: Learning to Love the Life I Already Have
recent_videos.description:
I don’t want my girls to remember a mom who was always waiting for the next thing to be happy.

I have plenty I’m still working on. But I’m trying to give the life happening in the meantime more of my attention. Time outside with my girls and the dogs helps me do that. There’s less to keep up with and more room to just enjoy each other.

I hope they grow up remembering how much I loved spending this time with them. I hope I remember to show it on the ordinary days, too. 

My 7 year old twins absolutely kicked my butt today up 950 vertical feet (Van Cliff Trail). I am so proud of those girls.

What’s one thing in your life right now that you want to appreciate more?

#PrettySweetAcres #Motherhood #SimpleLiving #Gratitude

छत्तीसगढ़ में 58% आरक्षण से जुड़े मामले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट के हालिया आदेश को लेकर इस वीडियो में महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी दी गई है। मामला **Yogesh Kumar Thakur vs Guru Ghasidas Sahitya Avam Sanskriti Academy & Others** से संबंधित है।

आपके द्वारा साझा किए गए आदेश के अनुसार, आवेदन को 29 अक्टूबर 2026 को मुख्य सिविल अपीलों के साथ सूचीबद्ध करने का निर्देश दिया गया है। आदेश में उस दिन सुनवाई होने या मामले का अंतिम फैसला आने की स्पष्ट पुष्टि नहीं की गई है।

इसलिए वीडियो में आदेश की वास्तविक भाषा, मामले की पृष्ठभूमि और आगे की संभावित कार्यवाही को समझने का प्रयास किया गया है।

• आरक्षण नीति और भर्ती प्रक्रिया से जुड़े अपडेट जानने वाले विद्यार्थी
• छत्तीसगढ़ के सरकारी नौकरी के अभ्यर्थी

छत्तीसगढ़ में स्वामी आत्मानंद उत्कृष्ट अंग्रेजी माध्यम विद्यालय (SAGES) की भर्ती परीक्षा देने वाले अभ्यर्थियों के लिए यह वीडियो बहुत उपयोगी है।

अगर आपकी परीक्षा कंप्यूटर पर होने वाली है और आपको यह समझ नहीं आ रहा कि ऑनलाइन परीक्षा का इंटरफेस कैसा होता है, प्रश्न कैसे हल करने हैं, टाइमर कैसे काम करता है और उत्तर कैसे सबमिट करना है, तो यह वीडियो अंत तक जरूर देखें।

💻 **इस वीडियो में क्या-क्या समझाया गया है?**

✅ कंप्यूटर आधारित परीक्षा (CBT) का डेमो इंटरफेस
✅ परीक्षा के निर्देश (Exam Instructions) कैसे पढ़ें
✅ परीक्षा में कितने सेक्शन और प्रश्न हो सकते हैं
✅ टाइमर (Timer) और बचा हुआ समय कैसे देखें
✅ प्रश्नों को सही तरीके से Attempt कैसे करें
✅ उत्तर Save, Review और Submit करने की प्रक्रिया
✅ Negative Marking है या नहीं—आधिकारिक निर्देश कैसे जाँचें
✅ परीक्षा हॉल में क्या करना चाहिए और क्या नहीं
✅ परीक्षा में कौन-से दस्तावेज साथ लेकर जाएँ
✅ ड्रेस कोड और जरूरी सावधानियाँ
✅ ऑनलाइन परीक्षा के लिए महत्वपूर्ण टिप्स

🎯 **यह वीडियो किनके लिए उपयोगी है?**

• स्वामी आत्मानंद विद्यालय भर्ती (SAGES) के अभ्यर्थी
• छत्तीसगढ़ में होने वाली शिक्षक भर्ती के उम्मीदवार
• कंप्यूटर आधारित भर्ती परीक्षाओं की तैयारी करने वाले विद्यार्थी
• पहली बार CBT परीक्षा देने वाले अभ्यर्थी

⚠️ **महत्वपूर्ण सूचना:** इस वीडियो में दिखाया गया कंप्यूटर इंटरफेस समझाने के उद्देश्य से एक डेमो है। वास्तविक परीक्षा का इंटरफेस, सेक्शन, समय, नेगेटिव मार्किंग, सबमिशन प्रक्रिया और अन्य नियम परीक्षा आयोजित करने वाली संस्था के आधिकारिक निर्देशों के अनुसार अलग हो सकते हैं। परीक्षा से पहले जारी आधिकारिक सूचना एवं परीक्षा केंद्र पर दिए गए निर्देशों को अवश्य पढ़ें।

📌 वीडियो को अंत तक देखें, ताकि परीक्षा के दिन आप ऑनलाइन टेस्ट देने की प्रक्रिया को बेहतर तरीके से समझ सकें।

इस वीडियो में छत्तीसगढ़ व्याख्याता भर्ती परीक्षा की तैयारी के लिए शिक्षण शास्त्र (Pedagogy) एवं मनोविज्ञान के महत्वपूर्ण टॉपिक्स को आसान भाषा में समझाया गया है। परीक्षा की दृष्टि से इन अवधारणाओं को समझना और उनका सही उपयोग जानना बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है।

📌 **इस वीडियो में कवर किए गए टॉपिक्स:**

✅ 1. प्रासंगिक अंतर्बोध परीक्षण (TAT – Thematic Apperception Test)
✅ 2. बाल अंतर्बोध परीक्षण (CAT – Children’s Apperception Test)
✅ 3. शब्द साहचर्य परीक्षण (WAT – Word Association Test)
✅ 4. वाक्य पूर्ति परीक्षण (SCT – Sentence Completion Test)
✅ 5. MMPI – Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory
✅ 6. समाजमिति (Sociometry)
✅ 7. GAS – General Adaptation Syndrome एवं तनाव मॉडल
✅ 8. उदीपन / उदात्तीकरण (Sublimation)
✅ 9. युक्तिकरण (Rationalization)
✅ 10. बौद्धिकीकरण (Intellectualization)
✅ 11. विस्थापन (Displacement)

🎯 **यह वीडियो किसके लिए उपयोगी है?**

• छत्तीसगढ़ व्याख्याता भर्ती परीक्षा के अभ्यर्थी

recent_videos.title: "If he objects, he’s dangerous." Handling first-time internet meetups safely 🛑 #shorts #viralshorts
recent_videos.description:
When teenagers want to meet someone they've only talked to online, simply forbidding it can drive them to go behind your back.

Instead, enforce a public chaperone protocol. Drive them to a public café, sit across the room, and let their online friend's reaction reveal their true intentions. Safety first, without destroying open communication!

“If you forbid internet meetups they could go behind your back. Teach them the public chaperone protocol for their safety!”
Key Takeaways for Parents:
 Avoid Flat Out Forbidding: Banning online meetups entirely often pushes teens to hide their plans.
 The Public Chaperone Rule: Drive them yourself and arrange the first meeting in a public café where you can supervise from a distance.
 Test Their Intentions: A safe, genuine peer will understand; anyone who objects is a red flag.

recent_videos.description:
When teenagers ask for privacy to study with a partner, balancing their comfort with healthy household boundaries can feel tricky.

Boundaries aren't a sign of mistrust—they act as structural support to help teens easily maintain trust. By setting clear, non-negotiable rules with dignity, you foster mutual respect without shaming them.
“Boundaries aren't a lack of trust; they are structural support. Set clear, non-negotiable household rules with dignity.”
Key Takeaways for Parents:
 Respectful Compromise: Acknowledge their desire for a comfortable study space while holding firm on household rules.  
 Reframe Boundaries: Clarify that rules exist to make maintaining trust easier, not out of suspicion.  

 Offer Alternatives: Provide open, public spaces like the dining table or study if total privacy is needed.

name: The Nurturant Dialogues
description:
The Nurturant Dialogues is a learning and reflection space exploring childhood, education, emotional intelligence (EQ), and human development. We begin with real practice, starting from what children are actually doing in everyday learning environments, and draw meaning through observation and reflection. Learning is made visible through lived classroom experience rather than slogans or shortcuts.

Some dialogues explain what is unfolding in learning spaces and why it matters. Others sit with questions around care, play, emotional development, and adult responsibility. Together, they support educators, parents, caregivers, school leaders, and policymakers in seeing children and systems with greater depth.

Grounded in global early childhood research and respectful, child centred philosophies, we explore free play, care as curriculum, learning environments, and the long term impact of early experiences on wellbeing, resilience, and identity.

recent_videos.title: Hospital Setup, Design & Strategy
Don't Buy The Land — The Hospital Model Most Doctors Get Wrong
recent_videos.description:
Dr. Anand Sancheti trained as a cardiothoracic surgeon, built a cardiac unit from nothing in rural Wardha, and then stopped operating altogether — five years ago — to build NewEra Hospitals into a group that is adding 500 beds this year.

This is a conversation about what actually happens when a doctor decides to build. Not the inspiration, the mechanics: how you choose land, why he now argues you should lease a running hospital instead of buying land and building on it, what a bank asks for, how EMIs start before a single patient walks in, what investors check that has nothing to do with medicine, and what changes the day you start reporting to a board.

We also spend the first half on the medicine itself — what to do in the first hour of chest pain, how the stent-or-bypass call is really made, what awake open-heart surgery is like, and how a surgeon chooses between a mechanical and a tissue valve.

ABOUT THE GUEST

Dr. Anand Sancheti is a cardiothoracic surgeon and the Founder and Managing Director of NewEra Hospitals, Nagpur. He trained at KEM, Apollo Chennai and Royal North Shore in Sydney, returned to India in 2006, and started a cardiac surgery programme at a rural medical college in Wardha in 2009 — moving a nine-person team with him on day one. He co-founded NewEra in 2016 with a neurosurgeon and an interventional cardiologist. The group now runs multiple hospitals across Nagpur and Navi Mumbai, with transplant, neuro, cardiac, trauma and critical care programmes, and is working towards an IPO.

Male Menopause: ED & Stress: The Conversation Men Never Have
recent_videos.description:
Most men in India wait years before asking anyone about a sexual health problem. Many never ask at all.

In this episode, Dr. Sameer Gade sits down with Dr. Sanjay Deshpande — who left a post as Associate Professor of Community Medicine at GMC Nagpur in 2003 to build a full-time sexual medicine practice, and who was elected to the Maharashtra Medical Council this year — for a direct, plain-language conversation about the things men and couples aren't asking their doctors.

We cover male menopause (andropause) and why the name itself is misleading; why testosterone should be checked after 40; the dangers of over-the-counter testosterone and gym misuse; erectile dysfunction and why it is often the earliest warning sign of heart disease and diabetes; how doctors distinguish physical causes from psychological ones; how stress, alcohol, smoking and modern working life affect sexual function; what actually happens in a counselling session; what premarital counselling should involve; and the myths still doing real damage.

The episode closes with Dr. Deshpande on the Maharashtra Medical Council — what the body does, why its elections became political, and the ongoing homeopathy registration dispute.

His closing message is for two audiences. For the public: don't ignore a sexual problem, and talk to someone — your family physician will not misguide you. For doctors: if you treat diabetes, hypertension, heart disease or psychiatric illness, ask your patients about their sexual health. They will not raise it themselves.

This conversation is general education, not medical advice. Nothing here replaces seeing a qualified doctor.

Newsepick is your trusted partner to create a collaborative learning environment where technology complements the traditional learning environment to meet the dynamic needs of the AI and automation-driven world. Students learning journey gets captured like never before.

Newsepick is not just a tool; it's a movement towards redefining educational paradigms. Aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, our platform empowers schools to transcend traditional learning boundaries, facilitating a dynamic environment where students can engage, interact, and collaborate in meaningful ways.

In India, a country marked by economic disparities, many schools face significant challenges in providing access to collaborative learning environments. These challenges often stem from the high costs and extensive resources required for implementation. Newsepick addresses these barriers with an economically viable solution that can scale to unite the Indian education ecosystem at large.

name: The Present Teacher - Helena Hains
description:
Welcome to The Present Teacher.

This channel is for teachers who are done shrinking themselves to survive a broken system.

I’m Helena Hains, author of That New Teacher Next Door, and I help teachers question the status quo and build classrooms—and careers—that are sustainable, calm, and aligned.

Each week, this channel covers four core pillars:
• Teacher Interviews — choosing aligned schools, spotting red flags, and interviewing without shrinking yourself
• Classroom Setup — designing classrooms that support behavior, learning, and your nervous system
• Classroom Management — structure and leadership without burnout or control tactics
• Time Management — systems that help you leave on time without guilt

This channel is for the teacher who knows that working harder isn’t the answer—and never was.

Because the teacher next door doesn’t make herself small to make others comfortable.
She knows who she is.
She knows the impact she makes.
And she has the courage to go after it.

recent_videos.title: ADHD वाले बच्चों की परवरिश कैसे करें? माता-पिता के लिए 6 ज़रूरी कदम | Parenting Wisdom
recent_videos.description:
ADHD वाले बच्चों की परवरिश कैसे करें? माता-पिता के लिए 6 ज़रूरी कदम | Parenting Wisdom

क्या आपका बच्चा एक जगह बैठने में कठिनाई महसूस करता है, बार-बार ध्यान भटकाता है, जल्दी गुस्सा हो जाता है या बिना सोचे कुछ कर बैठता है? ऐसे व्यवहार को केवल शरारत या अनुशासन की कमी समझना सही नहीं है।

इस वीडियो में हम समझेंगे कि ADHD (Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder) वाले बच्चों को प्यार, धैर्य और सही मार्गदर्शन के साथ कैसे सहयोग दिया जा सकता है।

🌟 इस वीडियो में जानिए 6 ज़रूरी कदम:

1. आसान काम और नियमित दिनचर्या: बड़े कामों को छोटे, सरल चरणों में बाँटें।
2. सकारात्मक संवाद: बच्चे की बात सुनें और स्पष्ट निर्देश दें।
3. स्वतंत्रता को बढ़ावा दें: बच्चे को अपनी उम्र के अनुसार काम स्वयं करने का अवसर दें।
4. परिणामों से सीखना: गलतियों पर अपमानित करने के बजाय सही व्यवहार सिखाएँ।
5. एक और मौका दें: गलती होने पर सुधारने और दोबारा प्रयास करने का अवसर दें।
6. सही Parenting Mindset: बच्चे की कठिनाइयों को समझें और उसकी छोटी-छोटी सफलताओं की सराहना करें।

❤️ याद रखें, ADHD वाले बच्चों को केवल अनुशासन नहीं, बल्कि समझ, संरचना, प्रोत्साहन और आवश्यक सहयोग की भी ज़रूरत होती है।

यदि आपको लगता है कि आपके बच्चे को ध्यान, आवेग नियंत्रण या अत्यधिक सक्रियता से जुड़ी लगातार कठिनाइयाँ हो रही हैं, तो योग्य बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ या मानसिक स्वास्थ्य विशेषज्ञ से सलाह लें। सही मूल्यांकन और व्यक्तिगत सहयोग बच्चे के विकास में मदद कर सकते हैं।

बच्चे अपने शिक्षकों के व्यवहार, बोलने के तरीके, अनुशासन और दूसरों के प्रति दृष्टिकोण से बहुत कुछ सीखते हैं। शिक्षक के कुछ शब्द बच्चे का आत्मविश्वास बढ़ा सकते हैं, जबकि कठोर शब्द उसके मन में डर और हीनभावना पैदा कर सकते हैं।

इस वीडियो में हम जानेंगे:

- एक बेहतर शिक्षक की असली पहचान क्या है?
- बच्चों के व्यक्तित्व पर शिक्षक का क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
- डाँटने और समझाने में क्या अंतर है?
- बच्चों में आत्मविश्वास और अनुशासन कैसे विकसित करें?
- गलतियों पर बच्चों को अपमानित करने के बजाय उन्हें कैसे समझाएँ?
- एक सकारात्मक और सुरक्षित कक्षा का वातावरण कैसे बनाएँ?
- शिक्षक और अभिभावक मिलकर बच्चों के बेहतर भविष्य में कैसे योगदान दे सकते हैं?

याद रखिए, एक अच्छा शिक्षक केवल पाठ नहीं पढ़ाता, बल्कि जीवन जीने का तरीका भी सिखाता है।

यह वीडियो शिक्षकों, अभिभावकों और शिक्षा के क्षेत्र से जुड़े सभी लोगों के लिए उपयोगी है।

recent_videos.description:
क्या आप चाहते हैं कि आपका बच्चा सिर्फ पढ़ाई में ही नहीं, बल्कि जीवन की हर परिस्थिति में समझदारी से फैसले लेना सीखे?

इस वीडियो में हम समझेंगे समझदार बच्चे की परवरिश के 4 ज़रूरी Pillars, जो बच्चों में स्वतंत्र सोच, लचीलापन, भावनात्मक विकास और सही व्यवहार को बढ़ावा देने में मदद कर सकते हैं।

🌱 इस वीडियो में आप जानेंगे:

✅ बच्चों में स्वतंत्र सोच कैसे विकसित करें
✅ छोटी समस्याओं को खुद हल करना कैसे सिखाएँ
✅ बच्चों को अपनी भावनाएँ पहचानना और व्यक्त करना कैसे सिखाएँ
✅ माता-पिता अपने व्यवहार से बच्चों के लिए सही उदाहरण कैसे बनें
✅ बच्चों की हर समस्या तुरंत हल करने के बजाय उन्हें समाधान खोजने का अवसर क्यों दें
✅ रोज़मर्रा की छोटी आदतों से बच्चों में आत्मविश्वास और जिम्मेदारी कैसे बढ़ाएँ

recent_videos.title: 10 Daily Habits to Raise Self-Controlled Kids | Parenting Wisdom
recent_videos.description:
Are you worried that your child is spending too much time on mobile phones, tablets, gaming, or social media?

What if the real solution isn't just limiting screen time—but teaching children how to control their own habits?

In this video from Parenting Wisdom, we explore 10 simple daily parenting habits that can help children develop self-control, independence, creativity, emotional awareness, and better decision-making skills.

🌱 10 Daily Habits Every Parent Should Know:

1. Let your child experience boredom.
2. Have one meaningful conversation every day.
3. Give your child a challenging task.
4. Make physical movement part of daily life.
5. Teach age-appropriate responsibilities.
6. Read together and discuss stories.
7. Encourage curiosity and observation.
8. Give children opportunities to create.
9. Practise small acts of kindness.
10. End the day with reflection.

Children are growing up in a digital world where screens are everywhere. Instead of relying only on restrictions and parental controls, we can help them build the inner strength to make thoughtful choices—even when we are not around.

The goal is not to make children afraid of technology. It is to teach them to use technology wisely without becoming dependent on it.

💛 Remember: Don't just focus on reducing screen time. Build the child behind the screen.

Watch till the end and discover how small daily habits can make a meaningful difference in your child's development.

If you found this video helpful, LIKE, SHARE, and SUBSCRIBE to Parenting Wisdom for more practical parenting guidance.

Disclaimer: This video is intended for general parenting awareness and educational purposes. It is not a substitute for individual professional advice.

recent_videos.description:
Gen Z Kaun Hai? Baby Boomers Se Generation Beta Tak — Generations Ki Poori Kahani | Parenting Wisdom

Why are today's children so different from their parents and grandparents? Why do we hear terms like Gen Z, Millennials, Generation Alpha, and Generation Beta everywhere?

In this video, we explore the fascinating history of generations, how they got their names, and how changes in technology, society, culture, and childhood experiences have shaped different age groups.

✨ In this video, you will learn:

- What is a generation?
- Who are the Greatest Generation and Silent Generation?
- Why are they called Baby Boomers?
- What does Generation X mean?
- Why are Millennials also called Generation Y?
- What does the Z in Gen Z stand for?
- What are the other names for Gen Z?
- Who are Generation Alpha and Generation Beta?
- How has technology changed childhood across generations?
- What can parents learn from understanding generational differences?

A Parenting Wisdom Perspective

Every generation grows up in a different world. Understanding these differences can help parents build stronger connections with their children, understand their changing needs, and develop a more thoughtful approach to parenting.

Remember, generation labels describe broad trends, not every individual's personality or abilities.

Watch till the end and tell us in the comments: Which generation do you belong to, and which generation do your children belong to?

name: Praja Life
description:
Welcome to Praja Life — a living experiment in unschooling, experiential learning, and sustainable living based in Pune, India.

We are an unschooling family showing what happens when learning leaves the classroom and enters the real world. Through our channel, we document our own journey alongside the community initiatives we run:

🌾 Ek Din Ka Farmer: Hands-on organic farming where families learn where their food really comes from.
🏭 Praja Sawand (Industrial Visits): Taking kids and parents inside local factories, artisan workshops, and businesses to see real-world skills in action.
🏰 Experiential History & Science: Hands-on projects (like our Diwali Durg fort-building workshops) that turn engineering and history into physical reality.
💡 Unschooling & Alternate Learning: Honest, practical guidance for parents curious about homeschooling, digital detox, and self-directed education.

Subscribe to join us as we raise curious, resilient kids through nature, industry, and life experience.

name: Educación sin Tiza
description:
Bienvenid@ a Educación sin Tiza, un espacio para reflexionar sobre el aprendizaje desde distintos enfoques.
Aquí hablamos de lo que se aprende dentro y fuera del aula: desde experiencias cotidianas hasta ideas que no siempre están en los libros, pero que también forman parte del proceso educativo.
No despreciamos la escuela ni los contenidos tradicionales —los valoramos—, pero también creemos que el aprendizaje es más amplio, complejo y humano.
Este canal busca abrir conversaciones sobre el currículum oculto, la formación emocional, la convivencia, los valores, el poder, la motivación y todo eso que también educa… aunque no tenga nombre en el plan de estudios.
Si querés pensar la educación más allá de la tiza, este canal es para vos.
✍️ Aprender no termina con una nota. Y enseñar no empieza solo con una pizarra.

recent_videos.title: Validity vs Reliability vs Objectivity vs Norms vs Usability: Standardization (Parameters) of a Test
recent_videos.description:
💥 What makes a test a good test? 

Validity, Reliability, Objectivity, Norms, and Usability

इस video में हम Test Standardization के पाँच key parameters को simple, practical और exam-oriented examples के through समझेंगे:

1. Validity – क्या test वही measure करता है, जिसे measure करने के लिए उसे बनाया गया है?

2. Reliability – क्या test हर बार consistent results देता है?

3. Objectivity – क्या test के results personal bias से free हैं?

4. Norms – किसी student के score का meaning हम group की performance के साथ compare करके कैसे समझते हैं?

5. Usability / Practicability – क्या test को real classroom situation में practically use किया जा सकता है?

Video में इन concepts को Test, Measurement, Assessment & Evaluation, reliability के methods, validity, objectivity, norms, usability और item analysis जैसे important topics से भी connect किया गया है।

recent_videos.title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 Explained: Neutrinos and the IceCube Observatory
recent_videos.description:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Francis Halzen for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. He is the first sole winner of the Physics Prize in over 30 years.

Neutrinos have no charge and almost no mass, and they barely interact with matter. They can pass through the entire Earth without being absorbed, which makes them very hard to detect. IceCube, a detector one kilometre across buried deep in the ice at the South Pole, was built to catch them.

In this explainer, Nandita Jayaraj speaks with Sridhar K, a theoretical physicist who teaches at Azim Premji University. They discuss:

What neutrinos are, and why physicists first proposed them to explain missing energy in beta decay
The four fundamental forces, and why neutrinos feel only the weak nuclear force
Cosmic ray experiments, including the Kolar Gold Fields experiments that detected atmospheric neutrinos in 1965
How IceCube detects neutrinos through the faint light, called Cherenkov radiation, produced deep in the ice
Why the high-energy neutrinos IceCube found come from beyond our galaxy
How neutrinos open a new kind of astronomy, carrying information from the most distant parts of the universe

This video is part of the Azim Premji University Nobel Prize Explainers series. Watch the chemistry and the physiology or medicine explainers, along with every edition since 2023, on our channel.

#NobelPrize #NobelPrize2026 #Physics #Neutrinos #IceCube #Astronomy #AzimPremjiUniversity

recent_videos.title: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 Explained: Optogenetics
recent_videos.description:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, a method that uses light to switch specific brain cells on and off.

The human brain has billions of neurons, organised into circuits that control different functions and behaviours. Optogenetics lets scientists activate one circuit at a time, with far more precision than electrical or magnetic stimulation.

In this explainer, Nandita speaks with Asha Mary Joseph, a cell biologist who teaches at Azim Premji University. They discuss:

How Hegemann’s curiosity about a single-celled green alga, Chlamydomonas, led to the discovery of a light-sensitive protein
How Hegemann and Nagel showed that this protein, channelrhodopsin, could make frog egg cells respond to light
How Deisseroth used channelrhodopsin to study neurons, first in cultured rat cells and then in living mice
What optogenetics has shown so far about memory, sleep, hunger, thirst and other behaviours
Early research on restoring partial vision, on hearing, on addiction and on brain–machine interfaces, and how far these remain from treatment

This video is part of the Azim Premji University Nobel Prize Explainers series. Watch the physics and chemistry explainers, along with every edition since 2023, on our channel.

#NobelPrize #NobelPrize2026 #Medicine #Neuroscience #Optogenetics #AzimPremjiUniversity

recent_videos.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 Explained: Mirror-Image Molecules and the Origins of Life
recent_videos.description:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. What does that mean, and why does it matter?

Many molecules come in left-handed and right-handed forms that are mirror images of each other, much like a pair of cricket gloves. Living systems use only one form: the sugars in living things are right-handed and the amino acids are left-handed. In the laboratory, however, reactions usually produce both forms in roughly equal amounts. How did life come to choose just one?

In this explainer, Nandita speaks with Debobroto Sensharma, an experimental chemist who teaches at Azim Premji University. They discuss:

What chirality and homochirality mean
Earlier Nobel Prizes for asymmetric synthesis, in 2001 and 2021
Kagan’s discovery of the non-linear effect
The Soai reaction, in which a reaction amplifies a small excess of one form to almost 100 per cent
What these discoveries suggest about the origins of life, and what remains unanswered
Why making only one form of a molecule matters for medicines

This video is part of the Azim Premji University Nobel Prize Explainers series. Watch the physics and biology explainers, along with every edition since 2023, on our channel.

recent_videos.description:
The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 was a landmark legislation which came into force in 2006. In 2009 it was renamed as Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Act. It gave poor rural people the right to seek work from the Gram Panchayats and contribute to local development by building rural assets. For twenty years it was the most important rural development programme of India resulting in employment and rural assets. However recently the legislation has been replaced by a new Act known as VB-GRAMG. Therefore it is an opportune moment to look back at the twenty year journey of MGNREGA and ask what are the lessons one can draw from the experience? 

Watch this conversation as Debmalya Nandi, Faculty at Azim Premji University discusses what has been the learning from 20 years of MGNREGA and what is the way forward.

recent_videos.title: ANZSCO Skill Level Kaise Check Karein | NZ Visa 2026
recent_videos.description:
Aapki job ka ANZSCO skill level kya hai? Yeh sawaal New Zealand work visa aur residence ke liye bohot zaroori hai, lekin zyadatar log is par confuse ho jaate hain. Is video mein live screen par dikhaya gaya hai ki Stats NZ ki ARIA website se apni occupation ka skill level kaise check kiya jaata hai.

Is video mein aap seekhenge:

ARIA tool par apni job ka title kaise search karein
Search result mein dikhne wale level aur asli occupation level mein kya fark hai
Occupation ka six-digit code, indicative skill level, tasks included aur exceptions kahan dekhein
ANZSCO skill level 1 se 5 ka matlab kya hota hai
Apne asli kaam ko occupation ke tasks se kaise match karein

Zaroori baatein:

ANZSCO aapka personal skill level nahi batata. Yeh us occupation ke liye aam taur par zaroori skill level dikhata hai.
Immigration New Zealand ke mutabiq, search result mein job title ke saamne dikhne wala level occupation ka ANZSCO level nahi hota. Occupation kholkar hi level check karein.
Kuch occupations ko work experience ya qualification ke basis par higher skill level par recognise kiya ja sakta hai. Example ke taur par, INZ ke mutabiq Bricklayer ko kam se kam 3 saal ke experience par skill level 3 maana jaata hai.
ANZSCO ki jagah dheere dheere National Occupation List (NOL) aa rahi hai. AEWV ke liye kuch NOL occupations use ho sakti hain, jabki doosre visas ke liye abhi ANZSCO hi use hota hai. Agle video mein hum NOL aur ANZSCO ka fark samjhayenge.

Agar aap New Zealand mein kaam ya residence ke liye apply karna chahte hain aur apni occupation ka sahi code aur level confirm karna chahte hain, toh apne case ke liye personalised guidance lena behtar rehta hai.

Yeh video general information ke liye hai, individual immigration advice nahi hai. Kripya apna phone number ya email comments mein share na karein.

🔎 ARIA (Stats NZ) - apni occupation ka skill level yahan check kijiye: https://aria.stats.govt.nz/aria/#ClassificationView:uri=http://stats.govt.nz/cms/ClassificationVersion/hgbQw

recent_videos.title: NZ Job Offer Ke Baad Bhi Work Visa Decline? AEWV Rule
recent_videos.description:
What are the minimum skill requirements for a New Zealand Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV)?

Bahut se log New Zealand mein job offer milne ke baad maan lete hain ki Work Visa pakka ho gaya. Lekin Immigration New Zealand (INZ) job offer ke saath-saath aapki skills bhi jaanchta hai, aur yahin par kai applications decline ho jaati hain.

Is video mein aap jaanenge:

ANZSCO level 1 se 3 ki job ke liye INZ ki do minimum skill shartein: kam se kam 2 saal ka relevant job experience, ya NZQCF level 4 ya usse upar ki qualification
Woh ek condition jo poori na hone par dono shartein bekaar ho jaati hain: aapka experience ya qualification usi ya milti-julti field ya industry mein hona chahiye, jis job ka offer aapko mila hai
Bachelor's degree ya usse upar ki qualification ke liye raahat: woh kisi bhi field mein ho sakti hai
2 saal ka experience lagataar ya full-time hona zaroori nahi, lekin kul milakar 2 saal full-time ke barabar hona chahiye
Bachelor's se neeche ki qualification New Zealand ke bahar se ho, toh International Qualification Assessment (IQA) ki zaroorat pad sakti hai

recent_videos.description:

Partner of a New Zealander Work Visa kaun apply kar sakta hai
Partner of a Worker Work Visa mein partner ka kaun sa visa eligible hota hai
Partner of a Student Work Visa ke liye partner ka course kis level ka hona chahiye

Har case alag hota hai, isliye apni situation ke hisaab se sahi salah zaroor lein.

recent_videos.description:
The Rio Grande Valley is more than where UTRGV is located. It is who we are, who we serve, and why we are here.

Across our classrooms, clinics, laboratories, stages and playing fields, UTRGV is opening doors, advancing healthcare, driving discovery and preparing graduates to strengthen the communities that raised them.

Our promise is to keep improving lives and building what comes next, right here at home, for this generation and every generation to come.

UTRGV. The Valley’s University.

Learn more at https://www.utrgv.edu/thevalleysuniversity/

#UTRGV #TheValleysUniversity #RioGrandeValley


ABOUT UTRGV

The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) was created by the Texas Legislature in 2013 as the first major public university of the 21st century in Texas. This transformative initiative provided the opportunity to expand educational opportunities in the Rio Grande Valley, including a new School of Medicine, and made it possible for residents of the region to benefit from the Permanent University Fund – a public endowment contributing support to the University of Texas System and other institutions.

UTRGV has campuses and off-campus research and teaching sites throughout the Rio Grande Valley including in Boca Chica Beach, Brownsville (formerly The University of Texas at Brownsville campus), Edinburg (formerly The University of Texas-Pan American campus), Harlingen, McAllen, Port Isabel, Rio Grande City, and South Padre Island. UTRGV, a comprehensive academic institution, enrolled its first class in the fall of 2015, and the School of Medicine welcomed its first class in the summer of 2016.

recent_videos.title: Why Do Husbands Stop Finding Their Wives Attractive After Marriage? | Reality of Married Life
recent_videos.description:
Why do some husbands stop appreciating their wives' appearance just a few years after marriage? @ShakeelInspires #ShakeelInspires

In many households, women become so occupied with family responsibilities, household chores, and caring for everyone else that they struggle to find time for themselves. Their appearance may change, their bodies may change, and their hair may no longer look the way it once did.

But before criticizing your wife for these changes, ask yourself one important question: Her parents raised her and cared for her for years, yet she did not go through the same changes in just three or four years. So, what has changed after marriage?

Marriage is not just about physical attraction. It is about understanding, appreciation, emotional support, and sharing responsibilities. A wife deserves love and respect, especially when she is working hard for her family.

A loving husband does not simply criticize his wife's appearance; he helps create a life in which she can take care of herself, too.

recent_videos.description:
12 Frugal Habits in Japan 🇯🇵 inspired by Japanese frugal living, Mottainai, saving money, leftovers, simple meals, and everyday life in rural Tohoku. How many of these Japanese habits do you already follow?

Growing up in Japan, I learned that living frugally doesn't mean giving up good food or enjoying life. Sometimes it's simply about using what you already have, avoiding waste, buying simple ingredients, and turning leftovers into a delicious meal.

In this video, I'm sharing 12 frugal habits I learned growing up in Japan — from cooking rice in batches and making the most of leftovers to avoiding food waste, using affordable ingredients, and finding small ways to save money every day.

And yes… being frugal doesn't mean skipping dessert! 🍵🤣
There's always room in the budget for a little shiratama matcha dessert.

One of my favorite examples is turning simple ingredients into comforting Japanese meals like miso soup with leftover daikon and  natto okonomiyaki made with ingredients already in the fridge.

🌱 In this video:
• 12 Japanese frugal habits
• Mottainai — the idea of avoiding waste
• Saving money through everyday habits
• Cooking with leftovers
• Budget-friendly Japanese meals
• Simple living in rural Japan
• Natto okonomiyaki
• Daikon & tofu miso soup
• Making the most of what's already in your kitchen
• Finding joy in simple, affordable living

🍜 RECIPE — Miso Soup with Daikon & Tofu

  Ingredients (2 servings):
・Daikon — as needed, microwaved
・Dried wakame — a pinch
・Powdered dashi — 1 tsp
・Firm tofu — as needed, cubed
・Miso — to taste

Instructions:
① Add dried wakame and powdered dashi to water.
② Add microwaved daikon and dissolve the miso into the soup.
③ Add cubed tofu, cook through, and enjoy.

🥬 **RECIPE — Natto Okonomiyaki

Ingredients (1–2 servings):
・Rice flour or all-purpose flour — 100g
・Egg — 1
・Water — 100ml
・Shirodashi — 1 tbsp
・Cabbage — 150g
・Thinly sliced pork — 100g
・Nagaimo — as needed
・Natto — 1 pack (optional)

Toppings:

recent_videos.description:
Feeling a pulling sensation in your lower abdomen or noticing something unusual in your vaginal area? It could be a sign of uterine prolapse.

Uterine prolapse occurs when weakened pelvic floor muscles and supporting tissues allow the uterus to descend into the vagina. It is more commonly seen after vaginal childbirth or around menopause. Depending on the severity and symptoms, treatment may include pelvic floor strengthening exercises under a physiotherapist's guidance, supportive devices, or surgical intervention. Early medical evaluation can help determine the most appropriate treatment for your condition.

recent_videos.title: What Happens During Labour Induction? A Complete Guide
recent_videos.description:
Has your doctor recommended induction of labour? Here's why it may be necessary and what you can expect.

Induction of labour is a medical process used to help start contractions when delivering the baby is considered safer than continuing the pregnancy. It may be recommended in certain situations, such as prolonged pregnancy, high blood pressure, diabetes, restricted fetal growth, or when the waters break without labour beginning. Depending on the condition of the cervix, doctors may use medications, a balloon catheter, or an oxytocin drip to initiate labour. Importantly, induction does not always lead to a C-section, and many women can still have a vaginal delivery when conditions are favourable.

Dr. Sangeeta Gomes, HOD and Senior Consultant in Obstetrics, Gynecology and Fertility at BirthRight by Rainbow Hospitals, Electronic City, Bengaluru, explains when induction of labour may be recommended, the methods involved, and how doctors assess the safest delivery approach for mother and baby.

recent_videos.title: How does pregnancy affect your body's ability to control blood sugar?
recent_videos.description:
How does pregnancy affect your body's ability to control blood sugar?

During pregnancy, certain hormones produced by the placenta make the body's cells less responsive to insulin. To maintain healthy blood sugar levels, the pancreas needs to produce more insulin than usual. When the body cannot produce enough additional insulin, glucose builds up in the bloodstream, resulting in gestational diabetes. Women with obesity or a family history of diabetes may be more susceptible to these changes. Understanding these risk factors can help expectant mothers recognise the importance of regular prenatal screening.

Should you stop feeding your child when they have diarrhea or vomiting?

Children need proper nutrition and hydration even when they have diarrhea. If vomiting continues or your child cannot keep fluids down, consult a pediatrician rather than giving anti-vomiting medicines without medical advice.

recent_videos.description:
Are babies born through IVF different from babies conceived naturally? Here's what you should know.

The main difference between IVF and natural conception lies in how fertilisation takes place. During IVF, the egg and sperm are combined in a laboratory, and the resulting embryo is transferred into the uterus. Once pregnancy is established, the baby develops in the womb, just as in other pregnancies. Babies conceived through IVF can grow and develop normally, although every pregnancy requires appropriate monitoring based on individual health factors. IVF does not automatically mean that a different method of delivery is needed.

Had a C-section during your first pregnancy? Does that mean your next delivery must also be a C-section?

Not necessarily! Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC) may be possible for women who meet certain medical criteria. A planned vaginal birth after a previous C-section should also take place in a well-equipped hospital with experienced obstetricians and immediate emergency care available.

Not necessarily! Uterine fibroids are usually non-cancerous growths that develop in the muscular wall of the uterus. Their impact depends on their size, location, and whether they cause symptoms. Treatment is recommended based on individual symptoms and reproductive health needs, and surgery is not always necessary.

recent_videos.title: Should you sleep on your left side, right side, or back after an IUI procedure?
recent_videos.description:
Should you sleep on your left side, right side, or back after an IUI procedure?

The good news is that your sleeping position does not determine the success of IUI. During the procedure, specially prepared sperm is placed directly into the uterus, so standing, walking, or sleeping in a particular position will not cause the sperm to fall out. In most cases, women can return to their regular daily activities after IUI unless their doctor advises otherwise. Instead of worrying about your sleeping position, focus on following your fertility specialist's instructions and recommended care.

recent_videos.title: Frequent urination, lower abdominal pain, or a constant feeling that your bladder isn't empty?
recent_videos.description:
Frequent urination, lower abdominal pain, or a constant feeling that your bladder isn't empty? These could be signs of a urinary tract infection.

Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are common in women and may cause frequent urination, discomfort, lower abdominal pain, or blood in the urine. Factors such as inadequate hydration and sexual activity can contribute to the risk of infection. If left untreated, some infections may spread to the kidneys, causing fever, chills, and back pain that require urgent medical evaluation. Staying hydrated, maintaining good hygiene, and seeking timely medical care can help support urinary health.

Dr. Sangeeta Gomes, HOD and Senior Consultant in Obstetrics, Gynecology and Fertility at BirthRight by Rainbow Hospitals, Electronic City, Bengaluru, discusses the common symptoms and causes of urinary tract infections in women, along with the importance of early diagnosis, appropriate treatment, and preventive care.
